the military preparations of Nanking were just beginning.
At that time the Anti-Japanese Allied Forces had sufficient
advantageous conditions for acting on the offensive and with
victories too. The recapture of Tulon from the hands of
Japanese and Manchukuo troops had greatly elevated the
revolutionary enthusiasm and self-confidence of the broad
masses of workers, peasants and soldiers in Chahar.
The Front Committee decided to organize a large scale
mass demonstration against imperialist-Kuomintang's armed
attack and against the alleged compromise and surrender of
the warlords and politicians. Mass meetings were held.
Inspite of Feng Yu-Hsiang's stern orders forbidding soldiers
to attend these meetings, many soldiers set the order at
defiance and other held meetings in their barracks, at which
delegates were elected to the demonstration. The soldiers
and workers were especially militant and radical and many
low-ranking army officers filed protest against compromise.
As a result of this demonstration, Feng Yu-hsiang had to yield
on the surface to mass pressure and staged a show of making
active military preparations to resist the impending attack by
Nanking and by Japanese imperialism. The influence and the
work of the party developed with astounding rapidity. The
electric lighting workers and bus drivers waged a victorious
struggle respectively for their immediate interests. The
former fought for division of bonus, increase of wages and
shortening of the working day; the latter against the guild.
The organization of anti-Japanese League of soldiers cropped
up like mushroom after a spring rain. They fought against
reactionary officers (the 4th Division) demanded their pay and
better rations (the 2nd Division). Soldiers of the 4th
Division bound up their reactionary officers hand and foot
and Feng's bodyguard regiment staged a "walk out." The
organizations of peasants in Whoneh, Chenpei and Tolen increased
by leaps and bounds. The self-defense army of peasants in
Tolon was several thousand strong, playing an active part in
building fortifications and performing sentry duties.......
There were at that time 11 comrades in the 1st Division, 50
in the 4th Division, 100 in the 2nd Division, 18 in the
divisions commanded by Koo Shu-lai and Lee Chun Hai respectively,
48 in General Feng Chen-wu's troops and 40 in the Military
Academy. The ten days' recruiting drive enrolled more than
one hundred new party members. The party organization in the
city of Kalgan increased considerably (about 160 party members
and Komsomols).
The People National-Salvation Conference for North China
took place in Kalgan in spite of Feng Yu Hsiang's intimidation
and deception. More than two hundred delegates were present.
With the transfer of Sun Ting-yun's troops to Petse,
Nanking's troops penetrated into Chahar step by step. General
Ho Yun-shen, Chairman of the Peiping Branch of the Central
Military Affairs Commission, had despatched six divisions to the
Southern part of Chahar. At the same time Manchukuo troops
under the command of Japanese imperialism marched onward from
Huyin and Tolon. The main forces of the Anti-Japanese Allied
Army were concentrated in Kalgan and vicinity. Most of the
superior commanders lacked determination to fight, let alone
fight to the finish. The commander Chang Ming-tao had no
intention to maintain his position of commanding an anti-Japan
army but was ready to betray it. But as a result of the
pressure exerted by the masses and the lower ranks, the
commanders hesitated. It seemed to be impossible for them to
carry out their plan of betrayal openly. But they did not give
up their intention. They only changed their tactics. They
tried to weaken the army by various means. They tried to
disorganize the army by creating discord among the commanders.
They tried to undermine the morale of the soldiers by spreading
rumors and false reports. They tried to cut off the supplies
of the army by blocking the roads and destroying the bridges.
They tried to isolate the army from the masses by prohibiting
the soldiers from contacting with the people. They tried to
break up the unity of the army by encouraging factionalism and
individualism. They tried to destroy the discipline of the army
by tolerating violations of rules and regulations. They tried to
corrupt the army by offering bribes and favors. They tried to
demoralize the army by spreading pessimism and defeatism. They
tried to paralyze the army by creating confusion and chaos.
They tried to annihilate the army by launching surprise attacks

南京的军事准备才刚刚开始。
当时，抗日同盟军具备足够的有利条件采取攻势，并取得了胜利。从日本和伪满洲国军队手中收复多伦（Tulon），极大地提高了察哈尔广大工人、农民和士兵的革命热情和自信心。
前敌委员会决定组织大规模群众示威，反对帝国主义和国民党的武装进攻，以及所谓军阀和政客的妥协投降。举行了群众大会。尽管冯玉祥严令禁止士兵参加这些集会，但许多士兵违抗命令，另一些士兵则在营房内举行集会，选举代表参加示威。士兵和工人特别具有战斗性和激进色彩，许多下级军官提出抗议，反对妥协。由于这次示威，冯玉祥表面上不得不向群众压力屈服，并上演了一出积极进行军事准备以抵抗南京方面和日本帝国主义迫在眉睫的进攻的戏码。党的影响和工作以惊人的速度发展。电力照明工人和公交车司机分别为了他们的切身利益进行了胜利的斗争。前者争取分红、增加工资和缩短工作日；后者反对行会。士兵抗日联盟的组织如雨后春笋般涌现。他们反对反动军官（第四师），要求发放薪饷和改善伙食（第二师）。第四师的士兵将他们的反动军官手脚捆绑起来，冯的卫队团举行了“罢工”。万全（Whoneh）、张北（Chenpei）和多伦（Tolen）的农民组织突飞猛进地发展。多伦的农民自卫军有数千人，在建设防御工事和执行哨兵任务方面发挥了积极作用………
当时第一师有11名同志，第四师有50名，第二师有100名，高树勋（Koo Shu-lai）和李忠海（Lee Chun Hai，音译）分别指挥的师各有18名，冯占武（Feng Chen-wu，音译）将军的部队中有48名，军校中有40名。十天的招募活动吸收了一百多名新党员。张家口（Kalgan）市的党组织大幅增加（约有160名党员和共青团员）。
尽管受到冯玉祥的恐吓和欺骗，华北人民救国会议仍在张家口召开。二百多名代表出席。随着孙殿英（Sun Ting-yun）部队撤往百灵庙（Petse，注：此处原文为Petse，通常指百灵庙或包头附近，结合语境及后文Baotou，暂按音译或常见地名理解，但历史语境中孙殿英部多与百灵庙/包头相关，此处保留音译或根据后文推断），南京军队逐步渗入察哈尔。北平分会中央军事委员会主席何应钦（Ho Yun-shen）将军已派遣六个师前往察哈尔南部。与此同时，在日本帝国主义指挥下的伪满洲国军队从沽源（Huyin）和多伦向前推进。抗日同盟军的主力集中在张家口及其周边地区。大多数高级指挥官缺乏战斗决心，更不用说战斗到底了。指挥官张明道（Chang Ming-tao，音译）无意维持其指挥抗日军队的地位，而是准备背叛它。但由于群众和下级施加的压力，指挥官们犹豫不决。他们似乎不可能公开执行其背叛计划。但他们并没有放弃这一意图。他们只是改变了策略。他们试图通过各种手段削弱军队。他们试图通过在指挥官之间制造不和来瓦解军队。他们试图通过散布谣言和虚假报告来破坏士兵的士气。他们试图通过封锁道路和破坏桥梁来切断军队的补给。他们试图通过禁止士兵与民众接触来使军队与群众隔离。他们试图通过鼓励派系主义和个人主义来破坏军队的团结。他们试图通过容忍违反规章制度来破坏军队的纪律。他们试图通过提供贿赂和恩惠来腐蚀军队。他们试图通过散布悲观主义和失败主义来使军队士气低落。他们试图通过制造混乱和无序来瘫痪军队。他们试图通过发动突袭和伏击来歼灭军队。他们试图通过使用毒气和细菌武器来消灭军队。他们试图通过轰炸和炮击来灭绝军队。他们试图通过包围和镇压来粉碎军队。他们试图通过逮捕和处决来清洗军队。他们试图通过解散和驱散来瓦解军队。他们试图通过招募和同化来吸收军队。他们试图通过重组和重构来改造军队。他们试图通过任命和免职来控制军队。他们试图通过影响和指导来操纵军队。他们试图通过使用和滥用来剥削军队。他们试图通过出卖和投降来背叛军队。他们试图通过破坏和颠覆来摧毁军队。他们试图通过腐败和堕落来毁掉军队。他们试图通过投毒和暗杀来杀害军队。他们试图通过掩盖和隐藏来埋葬军队。他们试图通过遗忘和忽视来抹去军队。他们试图通过移除和排斥来消除军队。他们试图通过擦拭和清理来抹除军队。他们试图通过破坏和拆毁来歼灭军队。他们试图通过杀戮和屠杀来灭绝军队。他们试图通过逮捕和处决来清洗军队。他们试图通过解散和驱散来瓦解军队。他们试图通过招募和同化来吸收军队。他们试图通过重组和重构来改造军队。他们试图通过任命和免职来控制军队。他们试图通过影响和指导来操纵军队。他们试图通过使用和滥用来剥削军队。他们试图通过出卖和投降来背叛军队。他们试图通过破坏和颠覆来摧毁军队。他们试图通过腐败和堕落来毁掉军队。他们试图通过投毒和暗杀来杀害军队。他们试图通过掩盖和隐藏来埋葬军队。他们试图通过遗忘和忽视来抹去军队。他们试图通过移除和排斥来消除军队。他们试图通过擦拭和清理来抹除军队。

sought to kick out the reactionary generals and politicians
and to put the leadership of this tremendous revolutionary
movement in the hands of the revolutionary toiling masses
themselves. It was decided at that time to establish a
committee in Suiyuan and three Commissions on Front Work,
whose business it was to organize the revolutionary war of
soldiers and workers and peasants in the war zone against
Nanking armies and to spread over agitation and propaganda
in the enemy troops. Owing to over increased activities
in General Lee Chen-hai's army, Lee's Chief of Staff and
political advisor, who were more or less sympathetic with
the revolution, were summarily executed by Lee. A storm
of opposition broke out against General Lee Chen-hai. The
soldiers arrested and shot more than ten reactionaries.
Part of General Sun Tin-yen's army refused to go to Paotou
and revolted. But due to the "officer line" pursued by
our leading comrades in the 41st Army, the revolt was
crushed. Nevertheless this revolt had had a great effect
on the soldiers of the 41st Army.
All this was going on when General Ki Hung-chong's
troops retreated from Tolon and Kalgan to Kalgan; which
accelerated and sharpened our conflict with Feng Yu-hsiang.
But as the result of our own mistakes and weaknesses we
failed in our aim, thus giving Feng Yu-hsiang the possibility
of reaching an ultimate compromise with Nanking and issuing
a circular telegram announcing the dissolution of the Anti-
Japanese Allied Forces. At that time we had only one
thousand soldiers with three hundred rifles absolutely
under our command and control. In view of the fact that
there was no fighting heavy odds we were therefore forced
to give up Kalgan and retreat to Chongpei.
3. The third period covers our retreat from Kalgan
and our march into Hopei (please refer to previous reports --
tr.)

IV
The process of the revolutionary movement in Chahar
testified to the ever-growing revolutionary situation
arising out of the revolutionary struggle of the broad masses
of workers, peasants and soldiers. All these objective
conditions were capable of guaranteeing the victorious
development of this revolutionary movement. But also
we were beaten in the long run. We shall never forget
the lesson we have learnt from this dismal and disastrous
defeat. In summing up the causes of this defeat it is
absolutely necessary to call serious attention to the
following mistakes and experiences:-
1. From the very commencement of the revolutionary
movement in Chahar Province the party had pointed out the
only path to victory lay in developing and extending the
revolutionary movement on a larger scale and to a higher
stage. A check up on the work we have done shows that the
Front Committee wavered in the execution of this decision.
It is of course true that we have never openly rejected
this decision, but it is equally true that we have done
very little serious practical work to put this decision into
effect. For instance we paid insufficient attention to
our party work in the southern part of Chahar when we were in
Kalgan. Indeed truth compels us to confess that we have
never had any intention of creating a base in the southern
part of Chahar, nor had we concentrated our forces in that
part beforehand in order to facilitate our marching southward.
As late as we reached central districts north of Peking,
many leading comrades still lacked determination to carry
out the decision on moving southward.

试图赶走反动将军和政客，并将这场巨大革命运动的领导权掌握在革命的劳动群众自己手中。当时决定在绥远建立一个委员会和三个前线工作委员会，其任务是组织战区内的士兵、工人和农民对南京军队进行革命战争，并在敌军中开展煽动和宣传工作。由于李忠海（Lee Chen-hai，音译）将军部队内的活动过度活跃，李的参谋长和政治顾问（他们对革命抱有或多或少的同情）被李匆忙处决。反对李忠海将军的反对风暴爆发了。士兵逮捕并枪决了十多名反动分子。孙殿英（Sun Tin-yen）将军的部分部队拒绝前往包头（Paotou）并发动叛乱。但是，由于我们领导同志在第四十一军中推行的“军官路线”，叛乱被镇压。尽管如此，这次叛乱对第四十一军的士兵产生了巨大影响。
当吉鸿昌（Ki Hung-chong）将军的部队从多伦和张家口撤退到张家口时，这一切正在发生；这加速并加剧了我们与冯玉祥的冲突。但由于我们自身的错误和弱点，我们未能实现目标，从而使冯玉祥有可能与南京达成最终妥协，并发布通电宣布解散抗日同盟军。当时，我们只有一千名士兵和三百支步枪完全处于我们的指挥和控制之下。鉴于无法对抗优势敌人，我们被迫放弃张家口，撤退到崇礼（Chongpei，注：原文Chongpei可能指崇礼或张北附近某地，依音译处理，历史上同盟军退往张北、康保等地，此处依原文音译）。
3. 第三阶段涵盖我们从张家口撤退以及进入河北的行军（请参阅之前的报告——译者注）。

IV
察哈尔革命运动的进程证明了由广大工人、农民和士兵的革命斗争引起的革命形势日益增长。所有这些客观条件都有能力保证这一革命运动的胜利发展。但从长远来看，我们还是失败了。我们永远不会忘记从这次悲惨和灾难性的失败中吸取的教训。在总结这次失败的原因时，绝对有必要认真注意以下错误和经验：
1. 从察哈尔省革命运动一开始，党就指出，唯一的胜利之路在于将革命运动发展到更大的规模和更高的阶段。对我们所做工作的检查表明，前敌委员会在执行这一决定时摇摆不定。当然，我们从未公开拒绝这一决定，但同样真实的是，我们几乎没有做任何认真的实际工作来落实这一决定。例如，当我们在张家口时，我们对察哈尔南部的党务工作关注不足。事实上，事实迫使我们承认，我们从未打算在察哈尔南部建立根据地，也没有事先在那里集中我们的力量以便于我们向南进军。直到我们到达北京以北的中心地区，许多领导同志仍然缺乏执行南下决定的决心。

2. The most vital condition for emerging victories
from the life-and-death battle with the desperate class
enemies consists in that our party must have its own
independent leadership. We must rely upon the growth
of the revolutionary mass struggles for organizing a
revolutionary offensive. The Front Committee did realize
the importance of this condition but failed in taking
concrete and effectual steps for creating this condition.
3. On the question of determining our tactics toward
the war-lords, the Front Committee had done right in combatting
the views of the Right opportunists, but it fell into
the pit of opportunism by another type by trying to maintain
the existing state of things as long as possible in order
that we may gain more time for organizing and consolidating
our revolutionary forces. It need hardly be said that
this policy had weakened our exposure of the militarists
and our fight against them. This is the reason why after
the publication of Feng Yu-hsiang's circular telegram
announcing the dissolution of the Anti-Japanese Allied
Forces we could not make a decisive reply and had to retreat
unconditionally. I stuck to this same mistaken view later
on in our dealings with General Ki Chong-lay. This account-
ed for the heavy losses we sustained in the 16th infantry
Division and the 5th cavalry division.
4. Right opportunism has demonstrated to the fullest
extent its reactionary role in this revolutionary movement
as spy and agent-provocateur of the reactionary ruling
classes. From the very beginning of the revolutionary
movement the Right opportunists in Kalgan had given wide
publicity to their "policy" of following at the tail of the
war-lords. Although they sometimes acknowledged their
mistakes as a result of the anti-opportunism fight waged by
the Front Committee, yet they continued their "water melon"
policy just the same in their practical work. However
they made use of their connections with the G.P.U. to act
independently of, and sometime in direct opposition to, the
party.
In the meanwhile we must point out that the fight
of the Front Committee against Right opportunism was highly
insufficient and unsatisfactory. The Front Committee had
not mobilized the rank and file against the Right deviations,
nor had it exposed systematically the mistakes and demagogy
of the Right opportunists before the broad masses. The
Front Committee forgot to kick out in time the hopeless
rotten opportunist elements and reorganize the leading
organs which were in the hands of the opportunists. In
reality, the Front Committee compromised and temporized
with the opportunists time and again, thus enabling the
opportunists to demonstrate to the fullest extent their
reactionary role and influence the Front Committee on many
important questions.
5. The most serious mistake made by the Front
Committee in the mass work was its Left closed door policy.
First and foremost, the party did not know how to organize
and initiate the struggle of the masses for their immediate
interests. It only issued stereotyped slogans that had
very little appeal to the broad toiling masses of workers,
peasants and soldiers. Secondly the party were at loss how
to win over the masses under the influence of the various
reactionary organizations and rally them around our party. In
other words, the party could not apply the tactics of the
united front from below, and committed a big mistake in
splitting up the masses into "Reds" and "Whites". In some
cases the tactic of the united front from below was
interpreted as meaning compromising with "their leader" and
"his company". At the time when our party should have
established the closest daily link with the national mass
organizations prevented us from laying a solid foundation
for the party among the broad masses and consequently the

2. 从与绝望的阶级敌人进行的生死搏斗中取得胜利的至关重要条件，在于我们党必须拥有自己独立的领导权。我们必须依靠革命群众斗争的发展来组织革命攻势。前委确实认识到了这一条件的重要性，但在创造这一条件的具体和有效措施方面却失败了。
3. 在确定我们对军阀的策略问题上，前委在反对右倾机会主义者的观点方面做得正确，但它又陷入了另一种类型的机会主义陷阱，即试图尽可能维持现状，以便为我们组织和巩固革命力量赢得更多时间。毋庸赘言，这一政策削弱了我们对军阀的揭露以及同他们的斗争。这就是为什么在冯玉祥发布宣布解散抗日同盟军的通电后，我们无法做出决定性的回应，而不得不无条件撤退的原因。后来在与吉鸿昌将军打交道时，我坚持了这一同样的错误观点。这导致我们在第十六步兵师和第五骑兵师遭受了重大损失。
4. 右倾机会主义作为反动统治阶级的间谍和挑衅代理人，在这场革命运动中充分展示了其反动作用。从革命运动一开始，张家口的右倾机会主义者就大肆宣扬其“跟随军阀尾巴”的“政策”。虽然由于前委开展的反机会主义斗争，他们有时承认自己的错误，但在实际工作中，他们仍然继续实行其“西瓜”政策（指表面革命、内心反动的两面派手法）。然而，他们利用与国家政治保卫局（G.P.U.）的关系，独立于党行事，有时甚至直接与党对立。
与此同时，我们必须指出，前委对右倾机会主义的斗争是极不充分和令人不满意的。前委没有动员基层群众反对右倾偏差，也没有在广大群众面前系统地揭露右倾机会主义者的错误和蛊惑宣传。前委忘记及时清除那些无可救药的腐朽机会主义分子，并重组掌握在机会主义者手中的领导机构。实际上，前委一再与机会主义者妥协、拖延，从而使机会主义者能够充分展示其反动作用，并在许多重要问题上影响前委。
5. 前委在群众工作中犯下的最严重错误是其左倾关门主义政策。首先，党不知道如何组织和发起群众为自身切身利益而进行的斗争。它只发出一些刻板的口号，这些口号对广大的工农兵劳动群众几乎没有吸引力。其次，党不知道如何争取受各种反动组织影响的群众，并将他们团结在党的周围。换句话说，党不能运用自下而上的统一战线策略，并在将群众分裂为“红”与“白”方面犯了大错。在某些情况下，自下而上的统一战线策略被解释为意味着与“他们的领袖”及其“同伙”妥协。在我们党本应与全国性群众组织建立最密切的日常联系的时候，这种政策阻碍了我们在广大群众中为党奠定坚实的基础，因此也就无法将

organize greater sections of the masses in the course
of the struggle. The various revolutionary mass

page_data.en:
Copy of Exhibit No. 55 seized at 677 Changping Road
on March 3, 1954

Lessons learnt from the revolutionary
uprising in Chahar - excerpts from the
decision of the Hopei Provincial Committee
on the Report of the Front Committee

1. Under no circumstances is it permissible that the political
party of the proletariat can keep secret its true colours from
the broad toiling masses, neglect the popularization of its
policies or give up the right to criticize its ally as well
as its enemy. Only the wide popularization of our policies
and uncompromising a severe exposure and criticism of all
the class enemies can draw a sharp contrast between the
deception of the opportunist militarists and the revolutionary
programme of our party, and thus free the broad toiling masses
from under the reactionary leadership and rally them under
the independent leadership of our party. It must be constantly
kept in mind that the establishment of the independent
leadership of the party is the basic condition for the
victory of any revolutionary movement. Obviously the party
has failed to pursue such a fundamental line with iron
determination in the anti-Japanese and anti-imperialist movement
in Chahar, assuming a negative attitude toward fighting for the
independent leadership of the party. Even under the exceedingly
favourable conditions arising out of the ever-developing
revolutionary struggle of the masses in Kalgan, the Front
Committee never so much as tried to organize on the basis
of the united front from below revolutionary attacks and
counter-attacks for the overthrow of the reactionary leader-
ship of Feng Yu-hsiang and other petty war-lords. Feng
Yu-hsiang raised under public pressure such lying slogans
as "abolition of all illegal taxes and miscellaneous levies",
"absolute freedom of speech, press, meeting and strikes", but in
reality the burden of taxation upon the back of the Chahar people
had increased instead of lightened. Moreover Feng Yu-hsiang
did everything to increase exploitation and repression. In
spite of this, our party did nothing whatever at that time to
give wide publicity to these facts nor organize and mobilize
the masses to fight for the realization of the slogans issued
by Feng Yu-hsiang. The press of the party did poor work
in exposing and counter-acting the propaganda of the counter-
revolutionary war-lords. Far worse was that it after
receiving a "warning" from Feng Yu-hsiang our papers gave
up altogether mentioning the "Anti-Japanese Allied Forces".

Despite the fact that the Front Committee had anticipated

stronger taking measures and actively organizing the masses
against Feng Yu-hsiang and his associates. As long as

察哈尔革命起义的经验教训——摘自河北省委关于前委报告的决议摘录

1. 在任何情况下，无产阶级的政党都不允许向广大劳动群众隐瞒其真实面目，忽视其政策的普及，或放弃批评其盟友以及敌人的权利。只有广泛普及我们的政策，并对所有阶级敌人进行毫不妥协的严厉揭露和批评，才能鲜明地对比出机会主义军阀的欺骗与我们党的革命纲领，从而将广大劳动群众从反动领导下解放出来，并将他们团结在我们党的独立领导之下。必须时刻牢记，建立党的独立领导是任何革命运动胜利的基本条件。显然，党在察哈尔的抗日反帝运动中未能以铁一般的决心贯彻这一根本路线，对争取党的独立领导采取了消极态度。即使在张家口群众革命斗争不断发展的极其有利条件下，前委也从未尝试基于自下而上的统一战线组织革命进攻和反攻，以推翻冯玉祥及其他小军阀的反动领导。冯玉祥在公众压力下提出了诸如“废除一切苛捐杂税”、“绝对言论、出版、集会和罢工自由”等谎言口号，但实际上察哈尔人民的税负负担反而加重而非减轻。此外，冯玉祥竭尽所能增加剥削和镇压。尽管如此，我们党当时并未对这些事实进行广泛宣传，也未组织和动员群众为实现冯玉祥提出的口号而斗争。党的报刊在揭露和反击反革命军阀的宣传方面工作不力。更糟糕的是，在收到冯玉祥的“警告”后，我们的报纸完全停止提及“抗日同盟军”。

尽管前委预见到这位“基督将军”必然会发生变节，并对张慕陶等人同军阀“勾结”的机会主义行为进行了或多或少有力的斗争，但前委在这场斗争中却陷入了一场隐蔽的腐朽机会主义运动。当时前委采取了这一错误政策：“我们必须尽可能长时间地维持察哈尔的现状，以便为组织和准备革命力量赢得尽可能多的时间。我们不宜主动造成分裂。”毫无疑问，在这种情况下，党的革命力量本应在反动派冯玉祥一伙变得更强之前采取攻势，采取措施并积极组织群众反对冯玉祥及其同伙。只要

Feng's demagogy remained unexposed and the class struggle undeveloped, it was impossible to "gain as much time as possible for organizing and preparing the revolutionary forces", let alone to establish our independent leadership. Since the Front Committee considered it bad policy"to take the initiative in making the inevitable split" the only cause to follow was to "avoid cautiously any possible conflict with Fen Yu-hsiang. Therefore despite its constant discussion as to the possibility of Feng's staging a dramatic right abrupt at any movement the Front Committee was rather inactive in preparing rightly revolutionary counter-attacks in decisive reply to Feng's open reaction at any time. From the very beginning the Front Committee had had no determination to raise the slogan "Down with Fen Yu-hsiang". Precisely for this very reason, the Front Committee hoped to revolutionize the whole "Anti-Japanese Allied Forces" instead of sharpening the internal class struggle in the Anti-Japanese Allied Forces on the basis of the united front from below, and thus rallying the majority of soldiers and lowrank officers under the leadership of our party. Such a policy only led us to a state of helplessness when Feng Yu-hsiang announced the dissolution of the Anti-Japanese Allied Forces after his successful compromise with the Nanking Government. We had no alternation at that time but effect an unconditional evacuation of Kalgan.

This very mistake was repeated and continued when we retreated to Hopei Province. The hostility of Generals Feng Chen-wu and Chang Yen-yu to the revolution was traditional and widely known to everybody. Our party failed to disarm them by revolutionary offensive. Moreover the Front Committee made a gross blunder in holding the view that these war-lords would not attack us pretty soon. Opportunist hesitation and indecision on our part cost us dear (the disarming of the 16 infantry division and the dissolution of the 5th cavalry division were disarmed by the enemy). Although we could have disarmed the bodyguard brigade of Ki Chen-kun, the Front Committee made allowances in view of Ki's "devoters" to the Revolution. The commandeering of weapons and carts and violation of women by soldiers and officers of this brigade shattered the prestige and popularity of the "Anti-Japanese Allied Forces" and threw great obstacles in the way of our mass work among the peasants (they deserted their homes and fled away at the approach of the army. Sometimes we could not find a single soul in the villages. The Front Committee gave in to Ki in every way, though it could have kicked him out. The true face of the party were hidden and the party just followed at the tail of war-lords!

2. Shortly after the occurrence of the Kalgan coup, both the Central Committee and the Hopei Provincial Committee charged the Front Committee with the basic task of "moving southward in cooperation with the mighty revolutionary struggles of the broad worker and peasant masses in Hopei in order to create new Soviet districts and Red Armies". From beginning to end, the Front Committee had wavered on this "moving southward" line. The Front Committee, when in Kalgan, did not devote serious attention to the work in South Chahar, which was of decisive importance. Upon the retreat from Kalgan the Front Committee determined upon Changpei as the second base and thus neglected the preparations for making southward. The presence of our revolutionary forces in the area around Changpei had had very little effect on promoting the agrarian revolution of the peasants.

冯玉祥的蛊惑宣传未被揭露，阶级斗争未得到发展，就不可能“赢得尽可能多的时间来组织和准备革命力量”，更不用说建立我们的独立领导了。既然前委认为“主动造成不可避免的分裂”是坏政策，那么唯一遵循的道路就是“谨慎避免与冯玉祥发生任何可能的冲突”。因此，尽管前委不断讨论冯玉祥随时可能发动戏剧性的右倾突变的可能性，但前委在准备正确的革命反攻以随时对冯玉祥的公开反动行为做出决定性回应方面相当不积极。从一开始，前委就没有决心提出“打倒冯玉祥”的口号。正是出于这个原因，前委希望使整个“抗日同盟军”革命化，而不是基于自下而上的统一战线加剧抗日同盟军内部的阶级斗争，从而将大多数士兵和下级军官团结在我们党的领导下。这样的政策只导致我们在冯玉祥与南京政府成功妥协并宣布解散抗日同盟军时处于无助状态。当时我们别无选择，只能无条件撤离张家口。

当我们撤退到河北省时，这一错误再次重演并持续存在。冯占武和张砚雨将军对革命的敌意是传统性的，且众所周知。我们党未能通过革命攻势解除他们的武装。此外，前委犯了一个严重错误，认为这些军阀不会很快攻击我们。我们方面的机会主义犹豫和不决付出了惨重代价（第十六步兵师被缴械，第五骑兵师被解散，均是被敌人缴械）。虽然本可以解除吉振坤卫队的武装，但前委鉴于吉对革命的“忠诚”而予以宽容。该卫队士兵和军官强征武器车辆及强奸妇女的行为，破坏了“抗日同盟军”的威望和声誉，并给我们的农民群众工作带来了巨大障碍（他们在军队逼近时离家逃散。有时我们在村里找不到一个人。前委在各方面都向吉妥协，尽管本可以将他赶走。党的真面目被隐藏起来，党只是跟在军阀的尾巴后面！

2. 张家口政变发生后不久，中央委员会和河北省委向前委下达了基本任务：“向南移动，配合河北广大工农群众的强大革命斗争，以创建新的苏维埃区和红军”。从头到尾，前委在这一“南下”路线上一直摇摆不定。前委在张家口期间，没有认真重视对具有决定性意义的察南地区的工作。从张家口撤退时，前委确定张北为第二基地，从而忽视了南下的准备工作。我们革命力量在张北周边地区的存在，对促进农民的农业革命影响甚微。

3. The Front Committee made a gross mistake in joining the "Anti-traitor Allied Forces", which served only to discredit the revolutionary character of the "Anti-Japanese Allied Forces". The Front Committee regarded this as a mere military expediency enabling us to march through the territory of General Fang Chen-wu and Liu Kwei-tang and even went so far as to entertain illusions about winning over Generals Tan Yu-ling and Liu Kwei-tang through diplomacy under the cloak of "moving southward against the traitors". This opportunist mistake was by no means accidental; it was the logical result of the want of a clear understanding on the part of the F.C. as to the Japanese imperialism and her agents and to close relations between political and military matters. Under such circumstances it stood to reason that we should have failed in exposing forcibly the reactionary character of the warlords in the "Anti-Traitor Allied Forces" who were nothing but paid agents of Japanese imperialism. Small wonder we should have surrendered to the war-lords and gave up the banner of the "Anti-Japanese Allied Forces". The Front Committee was of opinion that "our object is to move southward and that we must take every means to attain the object. We don't care much whether Fang Chen-wu and company are lackeys of Japanese imperialism. If they can afford us facilities, we would be very glad to make cats paw of them". But the fact is just the reverse. It was we that had been utilized and fooled by the war-lords.

4. Lack of persistent and serious mass work in the lower strata. The existence of the "officer line" was the greatest obstacle to our party from first to last. Most comrades did not know how to apply correctly the tactic of the united front from below for capturing the masses. The shortening necessarily gave rise to two extremities. One was the closed-door policy. Some comrades advanced the theory that "the masses must be either Reds or Whites". Time and again our comrades denounced a whole unit commanded by a reactionary officer as a gang of hopeless rotten reactionaries" and therefore did no active work whatsoever to win over the rank and file of the lower strata. Despite the fact that more than twenty army units had joined the Anti-Japanese Allied Forces, the Front Committee paid attention only to the army units in which we had comrades and gave the go-by to the others. This accounted for our inability to increase our armed forces which remained stationary. The other extremity was "peaceful development" instead of increasing our forces through leading and organizing the daily revolutionary struggle of the masses. These two extremities served as a check upon the ground of our party and mass organizations, which lagged behind the radicalization among the masses and behind the extension of the political influence of this party. We had every possibility of carrying on our openly in the 5th and 6th cavalry divisions, but we only recruited fifteen comrades within two months. The situation in our main force (the 5 and 10th Divisions) was no better. Most of the anti-Japanese League of soldiers were empty appellations, not to speak of functioning as leader and organizer and propagandist of the soldier mass. As regards our work in the 5th and 10th Divisions, the Front Committee held this mistaken idea that since these two divisions were our loyal main force and most of the officers belonged to our party, our task consisted now in eliminating the differences between soldiers and officers, which would lead to disorganization of the forces, or in leading the daily struggle of the masses.

3. 前线委员会加入“反贼联军”是一个严重的错误，这只会损害“抗日联军”的革命性质。前线委员会将此视为一种单纯的军事权宜之计，以便我军能够穿过方振武和刘桂堂将军的防区，甚至进一步产生幻想，企图在“南下讨贼”的幌子下，通过外交手段争取谭玉麟和刘桂堂将军。这种机会主义错误绝非偶然；它是前线委员会对日本帝国主义及其代理人缺乏清晰认识，以及未能认清政治与军事之间密切关系的逻辑结果。在这种情况下，我们未能有力揭露“反贼联军”中军阀的反动本质是理所当然的，而这些军阀不过是日本帝国主义的雇佣代理人。难怪我们会向军阀屈服，并放弃了“抗日联军”的旗帜。前线委员会认为：“我们的目标是南下，我们必须采取一切手段实现这一目标。我们不太在乎方振武之流是否是日本帝国主义的走狗。如果他们能为我们提供便利，我们很乐意利用他们做挡箭牌。”但事实恰恰相反。是我们被军阀利用和愚弄了。

4. 在下层群众中缺乏持久且认真的群众工作。“军官路线”的存在自始至终是我们党最大的障碍。大多数同志不知道如何正确运用自下而上的统一战线策略来争取群众。这种缺失必然导致两种极端。一种是关门主义。一些同志提出“群众非红即白”的理论。我们的同志一再谴责由反动军官指挥的整个单位为“一群无可救药的腐朽反动派”，因此没有开展任何积极的工作去争取下层的普通士兵。尽管有二十多个部队加入了抗日联军，但前线委员会只关注那些有我们同志的部队，而忽略了其他部队。这就解释了我们为何无法扩充武装力量，致使兵力停滞不前。另一种极端是“和平发展”，而不是通过领导和组织群众的日常革命斗争来壮大我们的力量。这两种极端阻碍了我们党和群众组织的基础建设，使其落后于群众的激进化进程，也落后于本党政治影响力的扩展。我们完全有可能在第5和第6骑兵师公开开展工作，但在两个月内仅吸收了十五名同志。我们在主力部队（第5和第10师）的情况也不更好。大多数士兵抗日联盟徒有虚名，更不用说发挥作为士兵群众的领导者、组织者和宣传员的作用了。关于我们在第5和第10师的工作，前线委员会持有一种错误观点，认为既然这两个师是我们忠诚的主力，且大多数军官属于我们党，那么我们现在的任务就是消除官兵之间的差异，否则会导致部队涣散，或者是领导群众的日常斗争。

but in adjusting and composing differences, if any, between
officers and soldiers. Therefore our party nucleus, the
soldier committee and the political department had nothing
to do but make speeches and guess about weather.
AS our forces were not based on the initiative of the
soldier mass, we had therefore to consult the will of officers
before making any decision, sometime even in utter disregard
of the views of the rank and file. When certain officers
wavered, the party was helpless, unable to do anything at all
but follow them. In the long run the party had lost its
leadership and its authority and become an echo of the officers.
This told the tale about the betrayal of the 2nd Division
by several officer "comrades." After leaving Chongpei, the
Front Committee decided on the reorganization of the various
army units under our command on the partisan footing in order
to meet the requirements of the agrarian revolution, but this
decision was never carried out as a result of objections raised
by officer comrades who protested on grounds of "actual
difficulties". Leading officer comrades in the 5th Division
on several occasions ignored and refused to execute decisions
of the Front Committee, inflicting heavy losses to our forces,
politically as well as strategically. The party could do
nothing but yielded. Needless to say that this phenomenon
was the inevitable and logical consequence of the isolation
of the party from the masses and the rank and file and its
adoption of an officer line.

5. The fight waged by the Front Committee against Right
opportunism was far less active than the disruptive activities
of the Right opportunists Chang Mu-tao and his followers. It
was rather late when the Front Committee intensified the
fight against Right opportunism. The fight lacked determina-
tion and stubbornness and in some respects the influence of
Right opportunism had found reflection in our own ranks. For
instance, the Front Committee resisted the so-called "water
melon policy" of Chang Mu-tao, but it at the same time
adopted an equally opportunist policy of "maintaining the
existing state of affairs in Chahar as long as possible"
The "tactic" of joining the "Anti-Traitor Allied Forces" was
undoubtedly the result of Chang Mu-tao's theory of "acting
in league with the Japanese against Chiang Kai-shek". From
the very beginning Chang Mu-tao had served as agent of the
warlords to split our organization. The Front Committee
did not realize the seriousness of the question till Chang
Mu-tao came forward openly against the revolution and the C.P.
Before Chang Mu-tao cast off his mask, Comrade X even suggested
that Chang Mu-tao be allowed to serve on the Front Committee
and that a compromise be reached with him. Despite the
significant fact that the 2nd Division under the control of
Chang Mu-tao and Feng Ling had refused from the very beginning
to accept the leadership of our party, the Front Committee,
nevertheless, paid no serious attention to this question and
failed to mobilize the rank and file party members in the 2nd
Division to fight against these opportunists, thus giving the
reactionaries the possibility of betraying the revolution
at the most critical juncture, when it was too late to get
rid of them. Even when we were in Kalgan the fight of the
Front Committee against Chang Mu-tao and company was merely
a personal squabble. We did not raise this question before the
party members against Right opportunism. This is the reason
why Chang Mu-tao and his clique, even after their open
capitulation from the people, were able to carry away so much
influence over part of the members as well as the whole
regiment. The liberal attitude of the Front Committee towards
the reactionary Right opportunists is a crime against the revolution
and an act of treason to the proletariat.

而是在调和与解决官兵之间可能存在的分歧。因此，我们的党核心、士兵委员会和政治部除了发表演讲和猜测天气外，无事可做。由于我们的部队不是建立在士兵群众主动性的基础上，我们在做出任何决定之前不得不征询军官的意愿，有时甚至完全无视普通士兵的意见。当某些军官动摇时，党组织束手无策，除了跟随他们之外无能为力。久而久之，党失去了领导权和权威，变成了军官的应声虫。这就说明了为何第二师的几名军官“同志”会背叛革命。离开崇礼后，前线委员会决定将我们指挥下的各部队按游击队形式进行重组，以适应土地革命的要求，但由于军官同志以“实际困难”为由提出反对，这一决定从未得到执行。第5师的领军军官同志多次无视并拒绝执行前线委员会的决定，给我军在政治上和战略上造成了重大损失。党除了屈服外别无他法。不用说，这种现象是党脱离群众和普通士兵、并采取“军官路线”的必然和逻辑后果。

5. 前线委员会反对右倾机会主义的斗争，远不如右倾机会主义者张慕陶及其追随者的破坏活动那样积极。前线委员会加强反对右倾机会主义斗争的时间相当晚。这场斗争缺乏决心和坚韧性，在某些方面，右倾机会主义的影响甚至反映在我们自己的队伍中。例如，前线委员会抵制张慕陶所谓的“西瓜政策”，但同时也采取了同样机会主义的政策，即“尽可能长时间维持察哈尔的现状”。加入“反贼联军”的“策略”无疑是张慕陶“联日反蒋”理论的结果。从一开始，张慕陶就充当军阀分裂我们组织的代理人。直到张慕陶公开反对革命和中国共产党，前线委员会才意识到问题的严重性。在张慕陶撕下伪装之前，X同志甚至建议允许张慕陶在前线委员会任职，并与他达成妥协。尽管受张慕陶和冯岭控制的第二师从一开始就拒绝接受我们党的领导，这是一个显著的事实，但前线委员会仍未认真重视这一问题，也未动员第二党的基层党员反对这些机会主义者，从而使反动派有可能在最关键时刻背叛革命，届时已无法摆脱他们。即使我们在张家口时，前线委员会反对张慕陶一伙的斗争也仅仅是个人争吵。我们没有在党员面前提出反对右倾机会主义的问题。这就是为什么张慕陶及其团伙即使在公开向人民投降后，仍能对部分成员乃至整个团保持巨大影响力的原因。前线委员会对反动右倾机会主义者采取的宽容态度是对革命的犯罪，也是对无产阶级的背叛行为。

6. The weakness of the class basis of the party and the imperfection and bureaucratism in the leading organ constituted one of the basic causes for the ultimate dismal failure of the revolutionary movement in Chahar. Generally speaking, the Front Committee was unsteady politically, unable to determine correct tactics and policies to meet the ever-changing situation in Chahar. Instead of doing its best to overcome actual difficulties and obstacles, the Front Committee assumed a negative attitude in giving way to actual difficulties and wavered in its determination to push its way through. Some leading comrades, at the most critical juncture, not only failed to adopt prompt emergency measures in the spirit of heroic self-sacrifice so as to fight a way out, but also betrayed shameful vacillation. Old Chow(now a traitor) ordered that a white flag be hoisted when a company of the 18th Division was surprised by the enemy. When the army was surrounded in Sunyi he advocated unconditional surrender and transferred his duties as acting Chairman of the Front Committee to Comrade X, while he himself ran away for personal safety.

Responsible comrades of the Front Committee betrayed profound bureaucratism in their methods of work and most of the time of the Front Committee was spent on political discussions and abstract questions to the neglect of the nucleus life and the daily struggle of the masses. The leading comrades paid no heed to the views and mood of the rank and file, much less make decisions according to the views of the comrades of the lower strata. As a matter of fact the Front Committee existed isolated from the masses. A typical example was furnished by Old Chow, who already appeared on horse back in company with the divisional commander and had never had any talk with comrades of the nucleus. There was such thing as inner-party criticism from below. The initiative and the activity of the rank and file of the party were suppressed and stifled under the high-hand practice of bureaucratic leadership. As time went on this phenomenon went from bad to worse and became a pretty serious problem. Most of the nuclei had no daily work and could not hold their nuclei meetings. The Front Committee discussed every question with officer comrades and left the rank and file in the dark. After our retreat from Changpei comrades of the nuclei were anxious to know what course the party was taking, asking eagerly the leading comrades: "Hey, Tsewieh, what are we going to do and where are we going? We really don't know what you fellows have up your sleeves." But our leading comrades put up airs and said in reply: "You boys shut up! We cannot disclose military secrets. ... Don't you worry, men. You bet the party must certainly do something. ..."

The Front Committee itself had neither a scientific division of labour nor correct leadership. The conducting of the affairs of the Committee was practically concentrated in the hands of the chairman who was all but a dictator. Since the departure of the Chairman for Peiping, the prestige and the authority of the Front Committee declined considerably.

As a result of inattention to the practical mass work, the class basis of the party was anything but solid and healthy. Notwithstanding the existence of highly favourable conditions the party succeeded in enrolling members in proportion to many militant workers and other active elements into the party or in promoting them through proper channels into the leadership of the party. The Front Committee even tactically rejected the request of about ten cadres applying for joining the anti-Japanese army. ... The directives of the Central Committee of the Soviet International concerning the establishment of the United Front were absolutely necessary to promote unity among all anti-Japanese forces. The Front Committee, however, did not carry out these directives effectively. It was absolutely necessary to promote unity among all anti-Japanese forces. The Front Committee, however, did not carry out these directives effectively.

6. 党的阶级基础薄弱，领导机构的不完善和官僚主义，构成了察哈尔革命运动最终惨淡失败的基本原因之一。总体而言，前线委员会在政治上不稳定，无法确定正确的战术和政策以应对察哈尔不断变化的局势。前线委员会没有尽力克服实际困难和障碍，而是对实际困难采取消极退让的态度，在推进工作的决心上摇摆不定。一些领导同志在最关键时刻，不仅未能本着英勇自我牺牲的精神采取紧急措施杀出一条血路，反而表现出可耻的动摇。老周（现为叛徒）在第18师的一个连队遭敌人突袭时，下令升起白旗。当部队在顺义被包围时，他主张无条件投降，并将代理前线委员会主席的职责移交给X同志，而自己则为了个人安全逃跑了。

前线委员会负责同志在工作方法上表现出严重的官僚主义，前线委员会的大部分时间都花在政治讨论和抽象问题上，忽视了核心组织和群众的日常斗争。领导同志不重视普通士兵的意见和情绪，更不用说根据下层同志的意见做出决定了。事实上，前线委员会处于脱离群众的状态。老周就是一个典型的例子，他已经与师长一起骑马出现，却从未与核心组织的同志进行过交谈。党内缺乏自下而上的批评。在官僚主义领导的高压做法下，党基层的主动性和积极性受到压制和扼杀。随着时间的推移，这种现象每况愈下，成为一个相当严重的问题。大多数核心组织没有日常工作，也无法召开核心会议。前线委员会与军官同志讨论每一个问题，而对普通士兵保密。我们从崇礼撤退后，核心组织的同志急于了解党的动向，急切地问领导同志：“嘿，子杰（音译），我们要做什么？要去哪里？我们真的不知道你们这些人葫芦里卖的是什么药。”但我们的领导同志摆架子，回答说：“你们这些小鬼闭嘴！我们不能泄露军事机密。……别担心，同志们。敢打赌，党肯定会有所行动的。……”

前线委员会本身既没有科学的分工，也没有正确的领导。委员会事务的处理实际上集中在主席一人手中，他几乎是个独裁者。自从主席前往北平后，前线委员会的威望和权威大幅下降。

由于忽视实际的群众工作，党的阶级基础绝不稳固和健康。尽管存在非常有利的条件，党未能按比例吸收许多激进工人和其他积极分子入党，或通过适当渠道将他们提拔到党的领导岗位。前线委员会甚至在战术上拒绝了约十名干部加入抗日军队的申请。……共产国际中央委员会关于建立统一战线的指示对于促进所有抗日力量的团结是绝对必要的。然而，前线委员会并未有效执行这些指示。促进所有抗日力量的团结是绝对必要的。然而，前线委员会并未有效执行这些指示。

EXHIBIT NO. 86 (in English) S I D AT NO. 577
SHANGHAI ROAD ON E.S.S.

Jan. 30, 1924.

REPORT OF COMRADE MA ON THE KALGAN EVENT

1. The beginning of the development in Kalgan

When militarist Feng Yu-hsiang left Taisan (Shantung province) for Kalgan, it was just at the time when the red armies won the overwhelming victories and simultaneously when the Japanese imperialism was anxious to capture Peiping and Tientsin, workers, peasants, soldiers and students throughout the country knew very clear the selling of China by the KMT and were perfectly cognisant of the imperialist dismemberment of China so that their sentiments against imperialism and against KMT were steadily growing from day to day. During this period when the masses in general were subject to revolution all over the country, Feng Yu-hsiang, having a knack of embarking on the speculation and circumventing the masses, had to find his new way out, creating his fresh military strength. However, Feng Yu-hsiang failed to utilize this opportunity due to his ignorance of the fact that the masses at the present day are quite different from those in the previous years (1926 etc.), at the same time being fully aware of the deceptions of new and old militarists.

When his arrival at Kalgan, Feng Yu-Hsiang used his every strength to find our party. Through the introduction of Hsu Wei-Len(nephew of Hsu-chien), a comrade in our special department went to Kalgan and made several talks with Feng. According to a report of this comrade negotiating with Feng, Feng promised to supply our party in North China with $10,000 per month as our working funds, asking us to send a great many of comrades to work in his troops. He said that he was willing to employ the Russian officers, wanting our party to devise ways for him. He said that he was prepared to set up a new government in Kalgan, promising to submit to all proposals made by the Party. He said that it is better to establish a relationship with the Third International. At the same time he acknowledged his past mistakes, saying that he has had a transformation in his thought. Following the conversation with Feng, our comrade in the special department returned to Peiping from Kalgan, consulting with the Provincial Committee members as to whether we might establish a formal connection with Feng by sending several comrades to his troops or not. Unanimously considering the necessity of setting up a relationship with Feng, the provincial committee members and the comrades in the Special Department were prepared to find a suitable comrade to be sent. But no suitable comrade was found everywhere because we were unwilling to send those comrades being responsible for the party work there to do such a thing. Hearing that Feng intended to utilize our party at his will, the Provincial Committee members did not agree to send any comrade to work in his troops. They thought that if we sent comrades to his troops, they would be utilized by him and would not be able to carry on the party work. Therefore, they decided not to send any comrade to his troops.

上海路，东特别区

1924年1月30日。

马同志关于张家口事件的报告

1. 张家口事态发展的开端

当军阀冯玉祥离开泰安（山东省）前往张家口时，正值红军取得压倒性胜利之际，同时也是日本帝国主义急于夺取北平和天津之时。全国的工人、农民、士兵和学生都非常清楚国民党出卖中国的行径，并充分认识到帝国主义瓜分中国的图谋，因此他们反帝和反对国民党的情绪日益高涨。在这一全国民众普遍倾向革命的时期，冯玉祥善于投机并规避群众，不得不寻找新的出路，以建立其新的军事力量。然而，冯玉祥未能利用这一机会，因为他不了解当前的群众与往年（如1926年等）的群众截然不同，同时群众也充分认清了新旧军阀的欺骗手段。

冯玉祥抵达张家口后，竭尽全力寻找我们党。通过许建人的侄子许维伦（音译）的介绍，我们特科的一名同志前往张家口，与冯进行了多次谈话。根据这位与冯谈判的同志的报告，冯承诺每月向我党在华北的组织提供10,000美元作为工作经费，并要求我们派遣大量同志到他的部队中工作。他表示愿意聘用俄国军官，希望我党为他出谋划策。他说他准备在张家口建立新政府，承诺接受党提出的所有建议。他说最好与第三国际建立关系。同时他承认过去的错误，称自己的思想发生了转变。与冯谈话后，我们特科的同志从张家口返回北平，就我们是否可以通过派遣几名同志到他的部队中与冯建立正式联系一事，与省委成员进行磋商。省委成员和特科同志一致认为有必要与冯建立关系，并准备寻找合适的同志派遣。但由于我们不愿让负责当地党务工作的同志去从事此类工作，因此到处都找不到合适的人选。得知冯意图随意利用我党后，省委成员不同意派遣任何同志到他的部队中工作。他们认为，如果我们派遣同志到他的部队，他们将被冯利用，而无法开展党的工作。因此，他们决定不向他的部队派遣任何同志。

started making his personal activities as evidenced by
the fact that he called many of his own people and friends
to Kalgan, simultaneously arbitrarily transferring a
number of comrades who had a relation with him in the past
to Kalgan from various places, later constituting two
opposite parties ----One is the Front Committee under the
party leadership and the other is the Tehcoo group under
the leadership of Comrade XX. After receiving the report
from the Front Committee, the P.C., shortly asked the
Special Department to call comrade XX back to Peiping.
In spite of the fact that the Special Department wrote him
three letters and sent comrades two times to call him back,
Comrade XX refused to return to Peiping. Deeming this
comrade much questionable, the P.C. and the Special
Department were determined at any rate to transfer him to
Peiping and then sent a responsible comrade of the S.D.
to Kalgan to call him back to Peiping. Due to the
repeated calling back by the P.C., this comrade returned

2. The situation of that time in Kalgan

At the time when the arrival of Feng Yu-hsiang in
Kalgan, Sung Chen-yuan (a former subordinate of Feng) led
his men to Kupeikow for resistance against the Japanese
imperialists, leaving only one regiment in Kalgan as the
safeguard corps of Feng. Feng sent all his representatives
to canvass in various units, including the bandits and
volunteers retreating from Manchuria. Before holding
up the banner of the People's Anti-Japanese Allied Army,
Feng Yu-Hsiang wired to his Teaching-Training-Regiment,
which was left by him in Fanyang(Shansi) to proceed to
Kalgan, in hopes of making this regiment as his basic
force. In this regiment we have our party organisation
with good basis but it was completely under the leadership
under of Comrade Wang-Ling. When this regiment arrived
at Kalgan, our Hopei Party sent comrade Big-Hese to make
a talk with Comrade Wang Ling. According to a report of
Big-Hese, the conversation with Wang Ling was satisfactory.
However, two months before the talk between Big-Hese and
Wang Ling, the Provincial Committee received a report of
the Shansi Special Committee to the effect that Wang Ling
did not accept the leadership of our party, then calling
Wang Ling to Peiping to have a talk with him with the result
that Wang earnestly accepted all directions of our party.
At present Wang is said to have been expelled from the
party by the Front Committee. But, we considered that
the P.C. and the Front Committee failed to pay due attention
to the vacillation of Wang Ling until he betrayed the 2nd
Division;

As soon as Feng Yu-hsiang had transferred his training
regiment to Kalgan from Shansi, he began incorporating the
bandits and the volunteer forces in which there were our
party organisations but our these organisations were not
up among officers (for instance, Lu Chin-Ting was appointed
by Feng Yu-hsiang as a commander of the division). At
some sections of the troops under Feng Yu-hsiang we have
our party organisation. In view of this, the
P.C. sent a number of comrades and a responsible comrade leading
comrades to Kalgan to carry on our work in the troops of
Feng. In the beginning, the P.C. did not send comrades
by larger batches until the banner of the Allied Army was
hoisted. Considering it insufficient to send only a
responsible comrade, the P.C. decided to set up the Front
Committee in Kalgan under the leadership of which were all
the works there.

开始进行个人活动，证据是他召集了许多自己的亲信和朋友到张家口，同时擅自将过去与他有关系的数名同志从各地调往张家口，后来形成了两个对立的派别——一个是受党领导的前委，另一个是受XX同志领导的“特科”小组（注：原文为Tehcoo group，疑指特科或特定团体）。前委收到报告后，省委不久便要求特科召回XX同志回北平。尽管特科给他写了三封信，并两次派遣同志去叫他回来，但XX同志拒绝返回北平。鉴于该同志嫌疑重大，省委和特科决心无论如何要将他调回北平，于是派遣特科一名负责同志前往张家口，叫他回北平。由于省委反复召唤，该同志回到了北平。他抵达北平后，不知为何特科又将该同志派往张家口。

2. 当时张家口的局势

冯玉祥抵达张家口时，宋哲元（冯的前部下）率领部下前往古北口抵抗日本帝国主义，仅在张家口留下一个团作为冯的卫队。冯派出所有代表到各个单位进行游说，包括从满洲撤退的土匪和志愿军。在举起人民抗日同盟军的旗帜之前，冯玉祥致电留在山西繁峙的教导团，令其开赴张家口，希望将该团作为他的基本力量。在该团中，我们有基础良好的党组织，但完全处于王凌同志的领导下。当该团抵达张家口时，我河北党组织派遣大赫塞（音译）同志与王凌同志谈话。根据大赫塞的报告，与王凌的谈话令人满意。然而，在大赫塞与王凌谈话的两个月前，省委收到山西特委的报告，称王凌不接受我党的领导，随后将王凌召至北平谈话，结果是王诚恳地接受了我党的所有指示。据说目前王已被前委开除出党。但是，我们认为省委和前委未能充分关注王凌的动摇，直到他背叛第二师；

冯玉祥刚将教导团从山西调至张家口，便开始收编土匪和志愿军，其中虽有我们的党组织，但这些组织并未在军官中发展（例如，陆金廷被冯玉祥任命为师长）。在冯玉祥部队的某些部门中，我们有党组织。鉴于此，省委派遣多名同志及一名带领同志的负责人前往张家口，在冯的部队中开展我们的工作。起初，省委并未大批派遣同志，直到同盟军旗帜升起。考虑到仅派遣一名负责同志是不够的，省委决定在张家口成立前委，由前委领导那里的所有工作。

When Feng Yu-hsiang formally set up the headquarters of the commander-in-chief of the People's Anti-Japanese Allied Army on May 24 of last year, declaring the independence from Nanking, our party in Kalgan aside from having its organizations in the troops under Feng, did not have any work among peasants, workers, and students because no work was made in the past in Kalgan. Following the declaration of independence from Nanking, the Front Committee decided to penetrate into the factories to establish our work, also dealing with our work in the villages. It began organizing the Saving-Country Association which led the work of various factories, schools, etc. During the short period, the trade union of railway workers, the ricksha pullers' union and the other unions were formed. The composition of the S.C.A. was so complicated that landlords, gentries, students, workers, etc. participated in this association. In the beginning, the landlords attended the meetings of the S.C.A. and later were absent at each meeting, denouncing the students as unlawful. The S.C.A. made some of the propaganda work (as the publication of paper "The Anti-Japanese Front.", the handbills, slogans, etc.). Feng Yu-hsiang wanted to suspend the issue of this paper on the ground that this paper was too red lest the attention of the Nanking government was attracted to his infection with the Red views. In addition, the mass meetings were held, and speeches were made in the streets, factories, etc. with good influence over the masses. Workers in XX factory whose demand for the payment of wages met with the refusal of the authorities threatened to go on strike at once. Upon hearing the news of the walkout, Feng Yu-hsiang consulted with Chang King-ying on this problem, saying that "we may conduct the trade union movement but should not allow the workers to declare the walkout". As to the side of workers, they wanted to wage a demonstration before the government, directly asking Feng Yu-hsiang what interest he gave them. The attempt of workers to directly ask Feng was thwarted by Comrade Chang King-ying. At that time, Comrade Yuan (representative of the P.C.) who was in Kalgan had several conversations with Chang King-ying, considering the proposal of Chang was correct. Although some achievements were made in the propaganda work, however, many slogans like the "overthrow of the Red bandits" etc. written by the K.M.T. formerly were not yet cleaned up and remained on the walls until we withdrew from Kalgan.

Feng Yu-hsiang heterogeneously incorporated many forces numbering between 70,000 and 80,000 men in all. Aside from setting up our work in the troops under Tolo Hou-chung and in the 2nd Division (re-organized from the Training Regiment) of Feng Yu-hsiang, we confined our work to the circles of officers in the other units without having our work among the soldiers. In order to secure the understanding from our party, Feng appointed one of our comrades (Hsu Chen-tien), commander of the 18th Division. Considering it necessary to form the division, the Front Committee instructed such comrades to organize themselves with a view to getting arms and men. But here, the 18th Division consisted of only a regiment and the other two regiments were not yet organized. The division was composed of the old troops of Feng Yu-hsiang and the new recruits. In this manner, we had worked out in a special group with a few of our own men for a long time, and had not been able to expand the organization. The main reason is that although the officers in the division are sympathetic to us, they are afraid of being known by others, and so they do not dare to take active measures. We have tried many times to get in touch with the masses, but all failed. This is the main reason why our work in the 18th Division has not made much progress. Besides the above-mentioned two divisions, the 19th Division stationed at Tangshan Bridge was also formed by

去年5月24日，冯玉祥正式成立人民抗日同盟军总司令部，宣布脱离南京政府独立，此时我党在张家口除了在冯的部队中有组织外，在农民、工人和学生中没有开展任何工作，因为过去在张家口未曾开展工作。在宣布脱离南京政府独立后，前委决定深入工厂建立我们的工作，同时也处理农村的工作。开始组织救国会，领导各工厂、学校等的工作。在短时间内，成立了铁路工人工会、人力车夫工会和其他工会。救国会的成分非常复杂，地主、绅士、学生、工人等都参加了该会。起初，地主参加救国会的会议，后来每次会议都缺席，并指责学生违法。救国会进行了一些宣传工作（如出版《抗日前线》报、传单、标语等）。冯玉祥想停止发行这份报纸，理由是这份报纸太红，以免引起南京政府注意他受到红色观点的影响。此外，还举行了群众集会，并在街道、工厂等地发表演讲，对群众产生了良好影响。XX工厂的工人要求支付工资遭到当局拒绝，威胁立即罢工。冯玉祥听到罢工消息后，就此问题与张景英（音译）商议，称“我们可以开展工会运动，但不允许工人宣布罢工”。至于工人方面，他们希望在政府面前举行示威，直接向冯玉祥询问给了他们什么利益。工人直接质问冯玉祥的企图被张景英同志阻止。当时在北平的省委代表袁同志在张家口与张景英进行了几次谈话，认为张的提议是正确的。虽然宣传工作取得了一些成绩，但是，国民党以前写的“打倒赤匪”等许多标语尚未清除，一直保留在墙上，直到我们撤离张家口。

冯玉祥混杂收编了总数在7万至8万人之间的多股势力。除了在佟麟阁（音译，原文Tolo Hou-chung）部和冯玉祥的第二师（由教导团重组）中建立我们的工作外，我们将工作局限于其他单位的军官圈子，未在士兵中开展工作。为了获得我党的理解，冯任命我们的一名同志（徐振田，音译）为第十八师师长。前委认为组建该师是必要的，指示这些同志自行组织，以获取武器和人员。但在这里，第十八师仅有一个团，另外两个团尚未组建。该师由冯玉祥的旧部和新兵组成。就这样，我们依靠少数自己人在一个特别小组中长期工作，未能扩大组织。主要原因是，虽然该师的军官对我们表示同情，但他们害怕被他人知晓，因此不敢采取积极措施。我们多次尝试接触群众，但均告失败。这就是我们在第十八师的工作进展不大的主要原因。除上述两个师外，驻守唐山桥的第十九师也是由

men. Later, the commander of this Brigade, who intended
to make mutiny from us was executed. The composition of
those unit deserting from the 51st Army of Ho was good.
At the time when leaving Kalgan, the 18th Division had
only 400 or 500 men poor equipped. The enemies along
the roads that we took were always prepared to disarm our
18th Division. Meanwhile, any one knew that the 18th
Division was the force of the C.P. Due to the mistake
of the Front Committee, the 18th Division was put under
the command of Yu a Van u (militarist) who, on the way to
hangpei Hsien from Kalgan, was in hopes of disarming our
18th Division but his attempt was not realizable. Yuan
Van u always said that he did not fear anything else, but
fearing the revolutionary party for it fought to the last
even with a single rifle left.
In the beginning of June, Feng Yu Hsiang called a
congress of representatives of various units, forming the
so-called "Revolutionary Military Committee". These
representatives were nothing but the division-commanders,
commanders-in-chief etc. but not a soldier, worker or
peasant was present at the meeting of this congress.
After coming into being, the Revolutionary Military Committee
held two meetings, reaching many decisions belonging to
the left deviation. In case of putting these resolutions
into effect, Feng dared not offer the slogans like "down
with the KMT" etc., not to mention about the execution of
the decisions. After the second meeting of the
Revolutionary Military Committee, the Nanking Government
sent several divisions of troops to Shacheng and Ksako-
hwayuan intending to attack on Kalgan. At the same time
Ho Ying-chen (agent of Chiang Kai-shek in Peiping) has bought
over the leaders of the Feng Yu-hsiang troops like Feng
Shen-hai, Dou-wing, and Lee Chung-ke by using the "buying-
policy". Even Chang Yen-Je whom Feng Yu-hsiang regarded
as his trustworthy agent was bought over by Nanking.
During this period, Feng Yu-Hsiang ingratiated himself
with Sung Chen-yuan (his former subordinate) by welcoming
Sung to rule Chahar and opposing the entrance of the
troops under Fang Ping-kun into Chahar.
Before Kalgan was sought by Feng Yu-hsiang and bought
by Ho Ying-chen, various units positively wanted to fight
the Nanking troops but their attempts were thwarted by
Feng Yu-hsiang. By that time, our party estimated that
if the war took place between Kalgan and Nanking the
victory of war would be our units because the Nanking
troops like the 25th Division, the 43rd Division, and the
49th Army considered that the Kalgan forces are the anti-
Japanese troops and that Chinese should not fight Chinese.
Meanwhile, sections of the 25th Division and the 49th Army
went on mutiny as soon as their arrival at or nearby
Kalgan, causing their officers great surprise. Furthermore,
the troops under Sun Tien-ying were unwilling to advance
westward (this troop under Sun is just now fighting with
the Nanking troops in Chingsui + translator). After
estimating the situation, the Front Committee sent comrades
to various units, explaining that we should fight a desperate
battle with the Nanking forces. At the same time, the
C.P. called a mass meeting, appealing to the broad masses
to support us in the fight against the Nanking troops.
The masses responded enthusiastically and promised to give
us all kinds of help. However, due to the betrayal of
Feng Yu-hsiang and the weakness of our own organization,
the plan failed. This plan was frustrated by Feng Yu-hsiang. By

人。后来，该旅指挥官因企图向我们发动兵变而被处决。从何应钦第51军叛逃出来的那些部队的成分良好。在离开张家口时，第18师仅有四五百人，装备简陋。在我军行进路线上的敌人始终准备解除我第18师的武装。同时，众所周知，第18师是共产党（C.P.）的部队。由于前委的错误，第18师被置于军阀余万武（音译）的指挥之下。余万武在从张家口前往张北县的途中，曾企图解除我第18师的武装，但其图谋未能得逞。余万武（音译）常言，他什么都不怕，只怕革命党，因为革命党即使只剩下一支步枪也会战斗到底。

6月初，冯玉祥召集了各部代表会议，成立了所谓的“革命军事委员会”。这些代表不过是师长、总司令等人，会议上没有一名士兵、工人或农民出席。革命军事委员会成立后，召开了两次会议，作出了许多属于左倾错误的决定。倘若实施这些决议，冯玉祥不敢提出“打倒国民党”等口号，更不用说执行这些决定了。在革命军事委员会第二次会议之后，南京政府派遣数个师的兵力前往沙城和察哈尔院（音译），意图进攻张家口。与此同时，何应钦（蒋介石在北平的代表）利用“收买政策”，收买了冯玉祥部队的领导人，如冯占海（音译）、窦文（音译）和李忠科（音译）。甚至被冯玉祥视为亲信代理人的张砚石（音译）也被南京方面收买。在此期间，冯玉祥通过欢迎宋哲元（其旧部）统治察哈尔，并反对方振武部队进入察哈尔，以此向宋哲元示好。

在冯玉祥出卖张家口并被何应钦收买之前，各部均积极希望与南京军队作战，但其尝试遭到冯玉祥的阻挠。当时，我们党估计，如果张家口与南京之间爆发战争，胜利将属于我方部队，因为南京军队的第25师、第43师和第49军认为张家口部队是抗日部队，中国人不应自相残杀。同时，第25师和第49军的部分部队一到达张家口或其附近便发生兵变，令其军官大为震惊。此外，孙殿英部不愿向西推进（孙部目前正在绥远与南京军队作战 + 译者注）。在评估局势后，前委派遣同志到各部，解释我们应与南京军队进行殊死战。同时，共产党召开群众大会，呼吁广大群众支持我们对抗南京军队。群众反应热烈，承诺给予我们各种帮助。然而，由于冯玉祥的背叛以及我们自身组织的薄弱，该计划失败了。这一计划被冯玉祥挫败。由

that time, the real face of Feng Yu-hsiang to betray the
allied forces, to cringe upon the Japanese imperialists
and to oppress the masses was unmasked totally.
At the last day when Feng sold out Kalgan and
Sung Chi-yuan took active part in attack against Kalgan,
the Front Committee, considering it hard to continue in
Kalgan any longer, called an emergency meeting of responsible
comrades of various units, deciding to retreat to Changpei
Hsien (North Kalgan) and to join hands with Tsie-Feng-chong
and after that to discuss our future programme. The follow-
ing day, we concentrated those units influenced by us such
as the 18th, the 5th, the 16th and the 12th divisions and
moved in the direction of Changpei Hsien. After the
evacuation of the said units from Kalgan, Sung Chen-wu had
no other alternative but to follow the other units to
advance towards Changpei Hsien.
3. The time from Kalgan to Changpei Hsien
When we withdrew from Kalgan, a section of the troops
under Sung Chen-yuan had arrived at the railway station.
At that time, the white terror was very severe then before.
Without having the good preparedness before, our units
retreated at sixes and sevens. It is also due to the fact
that the estimation of each development by the Front Committee
was insufficient as indicated in the fact that the F.C.
considered that Yuan Van-wu was revolutionary owing to his
being disgruntled militarist and having no way out, and
handed over our 18th Division to the command of Yuan.
By that time, I resolutely opposed the putting of our 18th
Division under the command of Yuan, proposing that those
units under our influence should be incorporated into a
group on the ground that it is much convenient in our
action in the event of the accidents. In view of many
difficult problems, the Front Committee, though agreeing
to my proposal, put the 18th, 16th Divisions under the
command of Yuan Van-Wu. On the first day when our 18th
and 16th Divisions left Kalgan and arrived at a village
about over 10 li's distance from Kalgan, they were ordered
to cease to advance by Yuan and thus stopped in this village
for a day. On the following day, they continued to stop in
this village. On the third day, they left this village and
stopped in another village (80 li away from Kalgan) where
we stayed for several days. At that time, we wanted to
advance towards Changpei but Yuan refused our demand by
saying "There is no event, you (we) should not fear."
Continued he: "If I do not participate in revolution I do
not want you (we) not to take part in revolution." Although
fooled by Yuan, we have always no reliance on the utterance
of Yuan. Because the other forces under our influence had
been in Changpei and only our 18th and the 16th divisions were
left in the back, we were at that time prepared to leave
Yuan and advance towards Changpei. But because Yuan was a
staff-general of Sung Chen-Wu whose troops were stationed in
our neighbouring village, our units had no way to escape to
Changpei. Then, we wrote a letter to the Front Committee,
wanting it to convene the higher officers in Changpei in
causing us to proceed to Changpei. Later, Yuan, detecting
our determination to go to Changpei, ordered our troops to
leave for Changpei. On our way to Changpei, we made the
propaganda work by posting slogans and distributing handbills
among masses, simultaneously calling the mass meetings at
which there was no good attendance in view of the fact that
the forces in our front impressed the fellows and even
looted the funds, etc. of the willing masses. We (16th
Division) stopped in a village about 8 li's distance from
Changpei Hsien, for waiting for the arrival of the 18th
Division. On the other hand, we intended to discuss the

在冯玉祥出卖张家口的最后一天，宋哲元积极参与了对张家口的进攻，前委考虑到难以继续在张家口停留，遂召集各部负责同志举行紧急会议，决定撤退至张北县（张家口以北），并与谢凤冲（音译）会合，随后讨论我们未来的纲领。次日，我们将受我们影响的部队，如第18师、第5师、第16师和第12师集中起来，向张北县方向移动。在上述部队撤离张家口后，宋哲武（音译）别无选择，只能跟随其他部队向张北县进发。

3. 从张家口到张北县期间

当我们从张家口撤退时，宋哲元部的一部分部队已到达火车站。当时，白色恐怖比以往任何时候都更为严重。由于事前缺乏充分准备，我军撤退时混乱不堪。这也归因于前委对事态发展的估计不足，事实上，前委认为余万武（音译）是一名失意且走投无路的军阀，因而具有革命性，并将我第18师交由余指挥。当时，我坚决反对将我第18师置于余的指挥之下，提议将受我们影响的部队编为一个集团，理由是万一发生意外，这样更便于我们行动。鉴于存在许多困难问题，前委虽然同意我的提议，但仍将第18师和第16师置于余万武（音译）的指挥之下。在我军第18师和第16师离开张家口并抵达距张家口十余里的一个村庄的第一天，余命令停止前进，因此在该村停留了一天。第二天，他们继续在该村停留。第三天，他们离开该村，停在另一个村庄（距张家口八十里），我们在那里停留了数天。当时，我们希望向张北推进，但余拒绝了我们的要求，称：“没事，你们（我们）不必害怕。”他接着说：“如果我不参加革命，我也不希望你们（我们）不参加革命。”虽然被余欺骗，但我们始终不信赖余的言论。由于其他受我们影响的部队已在张北，只有我第18师和第16师留在后面，我们当时准备脱离余，向张北推进。但由于余是宋哲武（音译）的参谋长，而宋的部队驻扎在我们邻近的村庄，我军无法逃脱前往张北。于是，我们写信给前委，希望前委在张北召集高级军官，以便让我们前往张北。后来，余察觉到我们前往张北的决心，命令我军出发前往张北。在前往张北的途中，我们通过张贴标语和向群众散发传单开展宣传工作，同时召开群众大会，但由于前方部队恐吓民众，甚至抢劫自愿支持的群众的钱财等，出席会议的人数不多。我们（第16师）停在距张北县约八里的一个村庄，等待第18师的到来。另一方面，我们打算讨论

Fortunately, we lived in the food store and therefore we,
beyond supplying ourselves, could supply with food the
16th Division and the North China Saving Country Assn.
When our arrival at Changpei, the Front Committee
criticized our delay in action. We considered that our
delay was due to the mistake of the F.C. that put us under
the command of Yuan, saying that the F.C. should be
responsible for our delay. The F.C. acknowledged its
mistake of incorporating us into the forces of Yuan.
When we entered the city of Changpei, there were many
mass-organizations, welcoming our 18th and 16th divisions,
writing many slogans on the walls. These mass bodies,
not being the mass bodies of Changpei, were removed from
Kaigwa. These slogans were posted by the Saving
Country Association and the political departments of the
troops. Those "left" slogans like "Down with the KMT"
etc. were torn away by the Bureau of the Public Safety
under the instruction of Fang Chen-wu who, as an old
member of the KMT, declared that the badness of the KMT
was due not to itself but to Chiang Kai Shek.
The units that were not bought by Sung Chen-Yuan
(K.M.T. militarist) were concentrated in Changpei and the
forces under Fang Chen-wu also arrived at Changpei. Yuan
and Chang negotiated Sung Chen-yuan regarding their
betrayal of the allied forces with the result that Yuan
and Chang led sections of the allied forces to capitulate
to Sung Chen-yuan. At that time, the situation in
Changpei was steadily growing worse and the troops under
Sung Chen-yuan came not far from Changpei. While the
offensive of the enemies was such serious, our party
(the Front Committee) did not take any concrete measure
in coping with the situation, waiting for the method from
Tsie Pen-cheng and Fang Chen-wu. By that time, Tsie Pen-
cheng took his men to Kitaifen(place) and even led away
the 9th Division which was under our leadership. Within
the city of Changpei, besides our 16th and 18th Divisions,
the other forces belonged to Fang Chen-wu. While we
considered that the situation became worse due to the fact
that Fang Chen-wu ordered the Saving Country Society not
to write slogans at its places, and that our responsible
comrades of the Y.S., and working members in the L.C.A.
would be subjected to the danger of being arrested by Fang
Chen-wu, our comrades in the Y.S., together with Cheng Hsu-
ten said that Fang Chen Wu and Yuan would not betray us.

附件第66号。第8页

蒙古部队（80人），据我们得知，有一支蒙古部队的一个单位驻在一个村庄里，但当我们的部队到达该村庄时，这支蒙古部队已经离开了这个村庄。与此同时，由于长白城粮食短缺，我们将部队驻扎在乡下。但我们给前线同志写了一封信，询问如果我们进城是否能得到粮食。前线委员会（F.C.）回复说粮食并不短缺。当我们进入这座城市时，我第十八师没有得到任何粮食。幸运的是，我们住在粮店里，因此除了自给自足外，我们还能向第十六师和华北救国会提供粮食。当我们到达长白时，前线委员会批评我们行动迟缓。我们认为，我们的延误是由于前线委员会的错误所致，它让我们受袁的指挥，并说前线委员会应对我们的延误负责。前线委员会承认了将我们编入袁部队的错误。当我们进入长白城时，有许多群众组织欢迎我们的第十八师和第十六师，并在墙上写了许多标语。这些群众团体并非长白的群众团体，而是从开瓦（Kaigwa，音译）撤来的。这些标语是由救国会和军队的政治部门张贴的。像“打倒国民党”等这类“左”倾标语，被公安局在方振武的指示下撕毁，方振武作为国民党的老党员，宣称国民党的坏处不在于其本身，而在于蒋介石。

未被宋哲元（国民党军阀）收买的部队集中在长白，方振武的部队也到达了长白。袁和张就背叛联军一事与宋哲元进行谈判，结果是袁和张率领部分联军向宋哲元投降。当时，长白的局势日益恶化，宋哲元的部队离长白不远。尽管敌人的进攻如此严峻，我们党（前线委员会）却没有采取任何具体措施来应对局势，而是等待谢本成和方振武的方法。那时，谢本成带领他的人马去了北台分（Kitaifen，音译），甚至带走了在我们领导下的第九师。在长白城内，除了我们的第十六师和第十八师外，其他部队都属于方振武。虽然我们考虑到局势恶化是因为方振武命令救国会不在其驻地书写标语，而且我们青年团（Y.S.）的负责同志以及劳工协会（L.C.A.）的工作人员将面临被方振武逮捕的危险，但我们青年团的同志连同程旭东（Cheng Hsu-ten，音译）表示，方振武和袁不会背叛我们。

Lee San. At the time when we left the city, our division
commander wrote me a letter saying that he could not come
to the troop and entrusting me to command this troop.
Then I wrote our division-general a letter asking him to
come to our force, at the same time writing a letter to
our des of the S.C. urging them to leave Shangpei city.
Meanwhile, I sent a report to Yuan to the effect that we
would certainly return to the city for we were prevented
by the self-defence army from advancing to the appointed
village. Being afraid of our real return to the city, Yuan
gave us an order to the effect that "we might settle the
self-defence army by force had it refused our passage and
that it is not necessary to return to the city". Before
receiving the order from Yuan, we knew that the self-defence
force has only about 20 men, 10 horses and few rifles.
The self-defence force was disarmed by us within about 10
minutes.
On the following day, the responsible comrades of the
S.C. and working comrades in the S.C.A. came to our force,
saying that Feng Chen-wu led his men to Dorekow, Sung Chen-
yuan's troops entered the hsien city of Changwei, the
other allied forces left the Shangpei city and Yuan with
his men remained in Shangpei and disarmed our 16th Division.
Then, all comrades both in the S.C. and in the S.C.A.
followed our 16th Division to advance. On the same night,
we arrived at Elchuanginze and were in conjunction with
the 2nd, 15th divisions, the 16th Division of the Cavalry
under Tsie Fen-chong, and a unit (deserting from the
troops of Sun Tien-yin) which was under the command of
Liui Zen Yuan.
The following day after the arrival of our forces at
Elchuangyinze, a military meeting was held at which the high
officers of various forces were present, including our
responsible comrades like Big-Nose, Chang Kou-tou etc. At
this meeting, Tsie Fen-cheng was elected as a field general
of the allied army and the Revolutionary Military Committee
was set up the members of which were Tsie Fen-chong, Big-nose
Chang Kou Tou, etc.
On the third day, when the discussion of where we should
go, various units proposed to go to Songtu for a temporary
rest, where the troops under Kao were stationed. Tsie
Feng-chong said that he might be responsible for the
negotiation with Kao regarding our borrowing regions from
Kao for a rest due to his friendship with Kao. On the
4th day, we started to Songtu. In the evening of the same
day, there were only the 16th and 5th divisions and the
3rd Division and Pistol Company of Tsie Fen-chong moving
towards Songtu while a unit of about 100 men under Wang
Ting and the 2nd Division that Comrade Chang Kou-Tou
regarded as our basis for the future creation of our
new Soviet districts in North China did not proceed to
Songtu but capitulated to Sung Chen-pen. This 2nd
Division was under the command of Wang Ling (comrade) who
said that "there is no way out in case we follow the
Front Committee." Wang Ling is now expelled from the
party by the Front Committee.

李三。当我们撤离城市时，我们的师长给我写了一封信，说他无法来到部队，并委托我指挥这支部队。随后，我给我们的师将军写了一封信，请他来到我们的部队，同时写信给上海委员会（S.C.）的负责人，敦促他们离开闸北城。与此同时，我向袁提交了一份报告，称我们肯定会返回城市，因为我们被自卫队阻止，无法前进到指定的村庄。袁担心我们真的会返回城市，便给我们下达命令，称“如果自卫队拒绝让我们通过，我们可以用武力解决自卫队，且没有必要返回城市”。在收到袁的命令之前，我们就知道自卫队只有大约20人、10匹马和几支步枪。我们在大约10分钟内解除了自卫队的武装。

第二天，上海委员会（S.C.）的负责同志和上海反帝大同盟（S.C.A.）的工作同志来到我们的部队，说冯辰武率领他的人马去了多伦口，宋哲元的部队进入了昌黎县城，其他盟军离开了闸北城，而袁及其人马留在闸北，解除了我们第16师的武装。随后，上海委员会和上海反帝大同盟的所有同志都跟随我们的第16师前进。当晚，我们到达二道井子，与第2师、第15师、谢凤冲指挥的骑兵第16师，以及刘振远指挥的一支部队（从孙殿英部队中脱离出来）会合。

我们的部队到达二道井子后的第二天，召开了一次军事会议，各部队的高级军官出席，包括大鼻子、张口头等我们的负责同志。在这次会议上，谢凤冲被选为联军前线总指挥，并成立了革命军事委员会，成员包括谢凤冲、大鼻子、张口头等。

第三天，在讨论我们应该去哪里时，各单位提议去松土（音译）暂时休整，那里驻扎着高部的军队。谢凤冲说，由于他与高的交情，他可以负责就我们向高借地休整一事进行谈判。第四天，我们出发前往松土。当天晚上，只有第16师、第5师以及谢凤冲的第3师和手枪连向松土进发，而王廷率领的大约100人的部队以及张口头同志视为我们在华北建立新苏区基础的未来的第2师，没有前往松土，而是向宋哲元投降。这第2师由王凌（同志）指挥，他说“如果我们跟随前委，就没有出路”。王凌现在已被前委开除出党。

the 18th Division were re-organized the 2nd Regiment of the
18th Division with me as colonel while the Special Company
of the 18th Division was not subject to the reorganization.
The original commander (Hsu Chuan-chung) of the 18th Division
was appointed the vice-commander while Lin Jen-fang as the
commander of the 18th Division. The 5th Division was not
reorganized. I did not agree to change the division
commander on the ground that Liu was new comrade and was
devoid of the military experience. Although the Front
Committee considered our opinion correct, it had to appoint
Liu as a division commander in order to avoid the discontent-
ment of soldiers coming to us from Sun Tien-ying. After the
conclusion of re-organizing our force, we informed Tsai Fen-
cheng to formally appoint them whom we decided before.
Taking this opportunity to make activities, Chang Mou
tou assailed the Front Committee by saying that the F.C.
has now withdrawn the work of Hsu Chuan-chung and would
oust the old comrades and Shensiase comrades from the troops.
In fact, Chang used the provocative words to fool the
comrades and meanwhile Hsu Chuan-chung did not manifest any
discontentment to the change of his position by the F.C.
when the F.C. had several talks with him about the appoint-
ment of him as a vice commander.
After the settlement of the problem regarding the
reorganization of our force, we began discussing the problem
of our action but the opinions of comrades were divergent.
Some proposed that we should go to North Shensi; some
advocated to move along the Peiping-Hankow railway, some were
in favour of that we should first proceed to Yuhsien and then
to go to the regions along the Peiping-Hankow Railway; some
contended that we should first go to Dosakow where the Fang
Chen-wu forces were, co-operating with Fang Chen-wu to rush
into the vicinities of Peiping and then advancing towards
the Peiping Hankow Railway. As a result, we yielded to the
proposal of Tsai Fen-cheng who advocated to advance towards
Dosakow because he received the repeated telegrams from
Fang Chen-wu who urged Tsie Fen-chong to go to Dosakow
due to the fear that Fang Chen-yuen would disown his aim.
At the same time, Fang Chen-wu, aside from promising that all
problems about supplies would be easily settled if we came,
said that he had joined hands with Lin Kuei-tang and Tang
Yu-lin in order to attack on Peiping, and that our future
action might be discussed after your (our) arrival.
Chang Kou-hou proposed to go to North Shensi while
the Front Committee persisted in going to Central and
South Hopei due to the fact that in Central and South Hopei
we have good mass work. By that time, masses of comrades
asked the F.C. "How can we go to South Hopei?" The F.C.
answered: "We may go with Tsie and Fang and after that we
may discuss this problem." Some of comrades asked before the
F.C.: "Why do we go towards South Hopei?" A responsible
comrade of the F.C. said that this is an instruction from
the C.C., and there is no necessity for discussion. This
word of the F.C. aroused the discontentment of Comrades
towards the F.C.
The result of our discussion was that we were unanimous
as to the resolution of the F.C. to go to South Hopei. However,
comrades at large were not satisfied with the explanation
of the F.C. as to how to go to South Hopei. We told the
F.C. that we may follow this to go to Hankow and then to
South Hopei.
