第18师进行了重组，我担任第18师第2团团长，而第18师的特务连未参与重组。第18师原指挥官徐传忠被任命为副师长，林任芳任第18师师长。第5师未进行重组。我不同意更换师长，理由是刘是新同志，缺乏军事经验。虽然前委认为我们的意见正确，但为了避免从孙殿英那边投奔过来的士兵产生不满，不得不任命刘为师长。在完成部队重组后，我们通知蔡凤成正式任命我们此前决定的人选。

张口头借此机会进行活动，攻击前委，声称前委现在已经撤换了徐传忠的工作，并将把老同志和陕西籍同志从部队中清除出去。事实上，张是用挑衅性的言论来愚弄同志，而当前委就任命他为副师长一事与他进行多次谈话时，徐传忠并没有对职位变动表现出任何不满。

在解决部队重组问题后，我们开始讨论行动问题，但同志们的意见存在分歧。有些人提议我们去陕北；有些人主张沿平汉铁路移动；有些人赞成我们先去蔚县，然后再去平汉铁路沿线地区；有些人争辩说我们应该先去多伦口，那里有方振武的部队，与方振武合作冲进北平附近，然后向平汉铁路推进。结果，我们屈服于蔡凤成的提议，主张向多伦口进军，因为他收到了方振武的反复电报，方振武因担心方振宇否认其目标而催促谢凤冲去多伦口。同时，方振武除了承诺如果我们到来，所有补给问题都将轻松解决外，还说他已经与林桂堂和汤玉麟联手进攻北平，并称我们未来的行动可以在你们（我们）到达后再讨论。

张口头提议去陕北，而前委坚持要去冀中和冀南，因为我们在冀中和冀南有良好的群众工作。那时，许多同志问前委：“我们怎么能去冀南？”前委回答：“我们可以随谢和方一起去，之后我们再讨论这个问题。”有些同志在前委面前问：“我们为什么要去冀南？”前委的一位负责同志说，这是中央的指示，没有必要讨论。前委的这番话引起了同志们对前委的不满。

我们讨论的结果是，大家一致同意前委去冀南的决定。然而，广大同志对前委关于如何去冀南的解释并不满意。我们告诉前委，我们可以据此先去汉口，然后再去冀南。

page_data.en:
The 5th and 18th divisions under our leadership,
together with the 3rd Division of the cavalry (about
1,000 men) of Tsie Fen-chong and his men (less than 1,000)
left for Dozekow. On the first day, our 18th Division,
on its way to Dozekow, met with the forces of landlords that
fired us in preventing us from passing. Thus, we ordered
our force to attack on the castle of the landlord militia
and within 3 hours the castle was captured by us. During
this operation, about 50 rifles, 30 horses, clothes and other
were wrested by us from the militias. Meanwhile, several
landlords were executed. The victory of this engagement
promoted the fighters to the high spirit for war.
Following the capture of this castle by us, propaganda
work was made. Properties of Church and landlords were
meted out to poor people, but the poor people dared not
take. On the way to Dozekow, beyond distributing handbills
among masses, we conducted the struggles for the division
of food. Some of villages were almost vacant and only
the aged and children were left at home, who said that all
men made their escape, fearing the arrival of Tang Yu-ling's
men looting our countryside.
Not far from Dozekow, we stopped in a village where
no food was found for the mass ran away in advance. In the
night, we were ordered to enter the city of Dorekow where
the forces of Tsie Fen-chong had come in while the men of
Fang chen-wu had left for Yenchow. In Yenchow, Fang Chen-
wu called a military conference of officers above the rank
of the division-commanders. A discussion was made regarding
the problem of the banner, resulting in doing away with
the banner of the Anti-Japanese Allied Army and in holding
up the flag of the Anti-Traitor Allied Army. At this
meeting Fang Chen-wu was elected as commander-in-chief;
Tang Yu-ling as vice-commander-in-chief; Tsie Fen-chong as
Field Commander of the Left Route, etc.
When leaving Dozekow, all forces were ordered to change
the anti-Japanese banner into the anti-traitor (Chiang
Kai-shek) banner. At that time, we heard that Fang, Tsie,
etc. stipulated for certain term with Japan and the Manchukuo,
many signs and small flags of which were distributed to
soldiers, causing them great hesitation. Scores of soldiers
asked our comrades by saying "Have we capitulated to the
Manchukuo? If true, we will wander away from the troops."
They have always shown hesitation, although we, under the
instruction of the Front Committee, explained before them
that this is our tactics. Their skepticism vanished until
the Japanese forces attacked us from the air.
In Dozekow where we had stayed for 4 days, the Front
Committee held a conference of our whole comrades, at the
meeting of which the F.C., aside from reporting on the
political situation of the present day, as well as on the
dismissal of Chang Kuo-tao from the party, did not make any
discussion regarding the other problems. Before this
conference was to be held, some comrades like Hsu Chuan-
chang did not agree to hold the conference of comrades,
on the ground that this issue is not the red army of present
and it would be detrimental to the morale even if the
conference of the party members be called. However,
Hsinglong rejected on him, saying that this issue should
not bring the red army at the present time, much less drive
the path towards the bad way, because it could not stand
at any time among the entire troops.
Some comrades, not informed by the Front Committee of
the holding of the party members' conference, asked the F.C.
whether they are members of the party or not and why the
F.C. did not tell them of the convocation of the conference
page_data.zh:
在我们领导下的第5师和第18师，连同谢凤冲的骑兵第3师（约1000人）及其部下（不足1000人），出发前往多伦口。第一天，我们的第18师在前往多伦口的途中，遭遇了地主武装的开火拦截，阻止我们通行。因此，我们命令部队攻击地主民团的城堡，并在3小时内攻占了该城堡。在这次行动中，我们从民团手中缴获了大约50支步枪、30匹马、衣物及其他物资。同时，几名地主被处决。这次战斗的胜利极大地鼓舞了战士们的士气。

在我们攻占这座城堡后，开展了宣传工作。教堂和地主的财产被分发给穷人，但穷人不敢接受。在前往多伦口的路上，除了向群众散发传单外，我们还开展了分粮斗争。有些村庄几乎空无一人，家里只留下老人和孩子，他们说所有男人都逃走了，害怕汤玉麟的人马来农村抢劫。

在多伦口不远处，我们在一个村庄停下，因为群众提前逃跑，找不到食物。夜间，我们奉命进入多伦城，此时谢凤冲的部队已经进城，而方振武的人马已前往燕京。在燕京，方振武召开了旅长级以上军官的军事会议。会议讨论了旗帜问题，结果是取消了抗日联军的旗帜，改举抗日贼联军（注：此处原文为Anti-Traitor，结合上下文及当时历史语境，实指反蒋或特定政治立场，译文直译保留原意）的旗帜。在这次会议上，方振武当选为总司令；汤玉麟为副总司令；谢凤冲为左路前线总指挥等。

离开多伦口时，所有部队奉命将抗日旗帜改为反贼（蒋介石）旗帜。当时，我们听说方、谢等人与日本和满洲国规定了某些条款，并向士兵分发了许多标志和小旗，导致士兵们极大犹豫。几十名士兵问我们的同志说：“我们是否已向满洲国投降？如果是真的，我们将离开部队。”尽管我们根据前委的指示向他们解释这是我们的战术，但他们一直表现出犹豫。直到日军从空中袭击我们，他们的怀疑才消失。

在多伦口停留的4天里，前委召开了全体同志会议。在这次会议上，前委除了报告当前的政治局势以及张国焘被开除出党一事外，没有讨论其他问题。在这次会议召开之前，像徐传昌这样的一些同志不同意召开同志会议，理由是这不符合当前红军的情况，即使召开党员会议也会损害士气。然而，兴隆反驳了他，说这个问题目前不应带入红军，更不应走向坏的方向，因为它在任何时候都无法在整个部队中站得住脚。

一些同志未被前委告知召开党员会议的事，他们问前委自己是否是党员，以及为什么前委不告诉他们召开会议

page_data.en:
Ex. 89. Page 10

of the party members if they were comrades. Some of
comrades asked the F.C. how we dealt with the converting
of the anti-Japanese banner into the anti-traitor banner
by Fang and Tsie. The answer of the F.C. was that it had
means after we followed Fang and Tsie to attack on Peiping.
At the meeting of the military conference held by Fang
in Yenchow, one of decisions was to advance towards Meeyen
etc. and to occupy Peiping before the 15th day of 6th
month by of the lunar year.

8. Action from Dozekow to Meeyen.
Following the men of Fang Chen-wu, our forces spent
about one week in their walking from Dozekow to Meeyen.
In the course of the travel, the F.C. did not discuss
our future method after the arrival at Meeyen, only follow-
ing the troops to walk. Despite the lack of shoes to wear
and food to eat, soldiers were in high spirit as walking,
hoping to have good prospects following the arrival of
their destination. Along the road we took, we never met
with a single peasant because the masses run away a long
time due to the fear of the bandits incorporated by Fang
Chen-wu into his forces.
The responsible comrades of the Front Committee explained
before comrades that they have decided our own measures and
effected our own independent military movement. However,
in fact, the F.C. did not do any preparatory work,
excepting limiting its work to the intercourse with the
high officers. Later, Fang Chen-wu informed us of the
arrival of his men at Kaeloeyen, wanting us to follow
them soon. Upon the arrival at a village (south of Hwei-
yuan), we heard that the men of Fang Chen-wu were defeated
by the K.M.T. troops and retreated from Kaeloeyen.
Meanwhile, a unit of the enemy cavalry attacked on our
force. During this period, our comrades in general asked
the F.C. what method our party would take. The F.C.
answered by saying that we will take our own way at night.
Arriving at Daishihko, the F.C. changed its original
line, wanting to proceed to East Peiping (East Hopei)
instead of South Hopei. At a place where the enemy
cavalry made ferocious attack on us, many comrades proposed
to wander away from Fang Chen-wu and Tsie Fen-cheng,
effecting our own independent military movement. That is,
they advocated to go to either South Hopei or various holes
east of Peiping. The Front Committee deemed it dangerous
to set up our independent movement so that it persisted in
not wandering away with Fang Chen-wu and Tsie Fen-cheng.

9. Details from Tushikow to Hajitown.
In order to avoid the attack from the enemy, our force
retreated to Tushikow. At the same night, our force left
for Hajitown where the responsible comrades of the Front
Committee ordered us to rush Shantungkow at 12 o'clock
in the following night in hopes of crossing the Peiping-
Shenyang railway and said that if we not leave this place
the enemy will send large units of the troops in checking
us from passing through Shantungkow. Due to the failure
of the 5th Division to arrive at Hajitown, we did not
begin conducting our military movement. On the third day
the enemy attacked on Hajitown. On the 4th day, we left
for Sungkow, intending to pass that place where the enemy
had sent large troops in preventing us from passing. Under
such circumstances, we were again prepared to retreat to
Tushikow and to go to Sockihshank through Sungkow. Just
at the time when we were starting, the 5th Division sent
a report to us, asking us to find a battlefield of the 5th
page_data.zh:
附件89。第10页

如果是同志的话，就属于党员。有些同志向前委询问，方和谢将“抗日”旗帜改为“反奸”旗帜，我们该如何应对。前委的回答是，在我们跟随方和谢进攻北平之后，自有办法。在方于燕郊召开的军事会议上，其中一项决定是向密云等地进军，并在农历六月十五日之前占领北平。

8. 从多子口到密云的行动。
跟随方振武的部队，我军从多子口步行至密云，耗时约一周。在行军途中，前委并未讨论抵达密云后的未来方针，只是随部队行进。尽管缺鞋少粮，士兵们仍士气高昂地行进，希望到达目的地后能有良好的前景。在我们经过的路上，未遇一名农民，因为民众早已因恐惧被方振武收编入其部队的匪徒而逃散。
前委负责同志向同志们解释称，他们已决定我方措施并实施独立的军事行动。然而事实上，前委除限于与高级军官交往外，未做任何准备工作。后来，方振武通知我们，其部队已抵达高丽营，要求我们迅速跟进。当我们抵达一个村庄（怀远以南）时，获悉方振武的部队被国民党军队击败，已从高丽营撤退。与此同时，一股敌军骑兵向我军发动攻击。在此期间，我们的同志普遍询问前委，我党将采取何种方法。前委回答说，我们将在夜间自行行动。抵达岱石口后，前委改变了原定路线，欲前往冀东而非冀南。在敌军骑兵猛烈攻击我处之地，许多同志提议脱离方振武和谢凤城，实施我方独立的军事行动。也就是说，他们主张前往冀南或北平以东的各据点。前委认为建立独立运动过于危险，因此坚持不脱离方振武和谢凤城。

9. 从土寺口到哈吉镇的详情。
为躲避敌军攻击，我军撤退至土寺口。当晚，我军前往哈吉镇，前委负责同志命令我们在次日午夜十二点急袭山屯口，希望能穿越北宁铁路，并称若我们不离开此地，敌军将派遣大部队阻止我们通过山屯口。由于第五师未能抵达哈吉镇，我们未开始实施军事行动。第三天，敌军攻击哈吉镇。第四天，我们前往松口，意图穿过敌军已派重兵把守以防我们通过的地方。在此情况下，我们再次准备撤退至土寺口，并经松口前往索什山。就在我们出发之际，第五师向我们发来报告，要求我们寻找第五师的战场

page_data.en:
Ex. 86. Page 11.
help it retreat for it had suffered a heavy loss with a
colonel being killed. Then we did to do so as it demanded.
At night when the 5th Division returned, we with it came to
Heishan, in the preparations for the second attack on
Toulinkow through where we might advance towards East
Peiping (East Hopei). Unexpectedly, the men of Fang
Shen-wu had been concentrated in Keishan, saying that it is
difficult to pass through Toulinkow because this pass is
guarded by the Japanese troops. In Heishan, Fang Shen-wu
held a military meeting at which the decision was reached
that there is no other alternative than to rush Shantungkow.
When we returned to Hojitown again, Big-Hoss (comrade) had
left our force for Peiping.
The responsible comrade of the F.C. said before us
that after passing through Shantungkow we certainly effected
our independent action, rushing across the Peiping-Suiyuan
railway and marching in the direction of the Peiping-Hankow
railway. Later when all of our allied forces repulsed the
enemy and passed Shantungkow, our units were ordered by
Tsie Fen-chong to advance towards the Peiping-Suiyuan
railway in attacking on a village where, about 20 li from the
railway, the unit of the enemy troops was stationed. After
the occupation of this village, we continued to advance
and arrived at a place about 10 li from the railway. By
that time, the whole of the 2nd Regiment of our forces proposed
not to go back but write a report to our army-commander,
asking him to concentrate all our forces in preparation for
crossing the railway and advancing in the direction of South
Hopei. Unexpectedly, the repeated orders came to our hands,
instructing us to return and saying that there is another
plan. In pursuance of the order from above, we then
returned. Later, the Front Committee sent a comrade to us,
saying that the preparation is made to leave Fang and Tsie
in the same night and to march towards South Hopei and
inviting us to express opinion. Our answer was that we
have none to express but quite agreed. Then, we ordered
our force to prepare for departure at 11 o'clock in the
night.
One hour after our force had been concentrated in the
playground, we did not see the arrival of our division-
commander together with the workers of the division-headquart-
ers. Then we sent many men to find our commander and
workers everywhere, discovering them still in sound sleep.
When our officers were awakened and came to the playground,
the 5th Division and the 15th Division were moving towards
Shantungkow in accordance with the order of Tsie Fen-chang.
Men were sent everywhere to find the 5th Division because
the F.C. lost its connection with the 5th Division. Therefore
we had to return and to advance towards Shantungkow in
pursuance of the instruction from Tsie Fen-chang. The
attempt to effect our independent action was not realized.
At 30 o'clock in the following morning after we arrived
in the vicinity of Shantungkow, the enemy positively fought
us and the 3rd Division of cavalry under command of Tsie Fen-
chang retreated after being defeated by the K.M.T. troops.
Then the 15th and 5th Divisions came to the rescue of their
fellow fighters. Being fully aware that we have no other
way but to fight, they and their men determined to launch
an counter-attack against the K.M.T. troops. The 15th and
5th Divisions were coming to a place at Hsiaho and
Shantungkow. When encountering the enemy, we started fighting
our forces found the main villages of the locality. While
we wanted to withdraw from the enemy in this situation, we
encountered a resistance from the enemy troops.
After the capture of Hsiaho, we stayed there about 4 or
5 days during which the F.C. did not make any statement.
Suddenly, comrade asked the F.C. what measures are being
taken. The F.C. answered that we should follow Fang
page_data.zh:
附件86。第11页。
以协助其撤退，因其损失惨重，一名上校阵亡。于是我们按其要求行事。夜间，当第五师返回时，我们随其来到黑山，准备通过头林口对冀东发起第二次进攻，由此可向冀东推进。不料，方振武的部队已集中在克山，称因该关口由日军驻守，难以通过头林口。在黑山，方振武召开军事会议，决定别无他法，只能急袭山屯口。当我们再次回到哈吉镇时，“大马”（同志）已离开我军前往北平。
前委负责同志对我们说，通过山屯口后，我们定能实施独立行动，跨越平绥铁路，并向平汉铁路方向进发。后来，当我联军全部击退敌军并通过山屯口后，谢凤城命令我军向平绥铁路方向推进，攻击距离铁路约20里、驻有一股敌军的村庄。占领该村庄后，我们继续前进，抵达距离铁路约10里之处。此时，我军第二团全体提议不再返回，而是向我军指挥官提交报告，请求集中全军力量，准备跨越铁路并向冀南方向推进。不料，反复的命令传达到我们手中，指示我们返回，并称另有计划。遵照上级命令，我们随后返回。后来，前委派一名同志前来，称已做好准备，将于当晚脱离方和谢，向冀南进军，并邀请我们发表意见。我们的回答是无可奉告，但完全同意。于是，我们命令部队准备在夜间11点出发。
我军在操场集结一小时后，未见师长及师部工作人员到来。于是我们派人四处寻找师长和工作人员，发现他们仍在熟睡。当我们的军官被唤醒并来到操场时，第五师和第十五师正按照谢凤城的命令向山屯口移动。由于前委与第五师失去联系，我们派人四处寻找第五师。因此，我们不得不返回，并按照谢凤城的指令向山屯口推进。实施独立行动的企图未能实现。次日凌晨30时（原文如此，疑为凌晨3点或笔误），当我们抵达山屯口附近时，敌军积极与我军交战，谢凤城指挥的骑兵第三师被国民党军队击败后撤退。随后，第十五师和第五师前来救援战友。他们充分意识到除了战斗别无他路，便与其部下决定对国民党军队发起反击。第十五师和第五师抵达下河和山屯口一带。遭遇敌军时，我军开始战斗，部队发现了当地的主要村庄。当我们想在这种情况下撤出敌军包围时，却遭遇了敌军部队的抵抗。
攻占下河后，我们在那里停留了约4或5天，期间前委未作任何表态。突然，有同志询问前委正在采取何种措施。前委回答说，我们应该跟随方

page_data.en:
No. 86. Page 12.

and this is to advance towards East Peiping, considering it impossible that our 18th and 5th divisions establish their independent movement. When we left Hulohe and advanced eastward, it was reported that the Japanese troops were there and it is difficult for us to pass. According to our investigation, there was nothing but rumour made by Fang Chen-wu who intends to surrender to Ho Yin-ching (agent of Chiang Kai-shek in Peiping), unwilling to make us wander away from him. Due to the hinderance by the Japanese force, our force had to return to Hulohe. When returning, we discovered that this village had been occupied by the enemy, and, after a bitter fighting, we recaptured Hulohe.

One day, in the early morning, the enemies launched an attack on all lines against Hulohe, with the support of the Japanese air forces. At that time, our shots and shells were nearly exhausted and our army commander Liu, considering we would be disarmed by the enemy unless we fight a desperate battle, sent a report to Fang and Tsie asking them what to do. Their answer was to "rush out." After getting the order, we prepared to begin rushing.

The order from Fang and Tsie said that they conducted the counter-attack on all lines. In fact, the 18th, 5th divisions, together with sections of the forces under Tsie and Fang, took part in the counter-attack against the enemy, with the result that within 3 hours the small and big hills (Toushan) were reoccupied by us and about one regiment of the enemy was disarmed.

After the recapture of Choutunshan(small hill) comrades in general considered it better to leave Choutunshan, either going to North or South. At the same time, they demanded the P.C. to concentrate our forces and those under our influence together in order to facilitate our actions. I, with comrades acting the political work in the troops, asked the P.C. what measure we should take. When visiting the P.C., we met with an opposition from our army-commander (Liu Tzu-Fung) who expressed an angry manner causing our extreme dissatisfaction. Seeing that the situation was not good, the P.C. called me out of the room, saying that Liu was very vacillating recently, and explaining many problems for us. However, I was not satisfied with such explanation.

Since we re-occupied Choutunshan, we stayed there for one week during which the enemies attacked on us everyday. In their attempt to surrender to Nanking, Fang Chen-wu and Tsie Pen-cheng every day dispatched their representatives to Peiping to consult with Ho Yin-ching(agent of Nanking) with regard to the capitulating terms while our P.C. viewed this problem with equanimity, waiting for the betrayal of Fang and Tsie. Every day, comrades visited the members of the P.C. and asked them whether we follow Fang and Tsie to surrender or we carry out our independent military action. The P.C. answered: "We leave for our destination tomorrow." Today our responsible comrades in the P.C. said "to-morrow" to go thereon to-morrow then said still "tomorrow." Of course such dilatory policy of the P.C. not only causes it to lose its confidence among comrades but also causes it to undergo dissatisfaction with it and in any case to no avail. In the end that the P.C. and our military leader (comrade Liu Chang-Jen) will follow in the wake of Fang Chen-wu and Tsie Pen-cheng to surrender to the enemy by selling out our 18th and 5th divisions.
page_data.zh:
编号86。第12页。

并向此方向前进，即向冀东推进，认为我军第十八师和第五师建立独立运动是不可能的。当我们离开葫芦河向东推进时，据报道那里有日军，我们难以通过。据我们调查，这不过是方振武制造的谣言，他意图向何应钦（蒋介石在北平的代理人）投降，不愿让我们脱离他。由于日军的阻碍，我军不得不返回葫芦河。返回时，我们发现该村庄已被敌军占领，经过激烈战斗，我们重新夺回了葫芦河。
一天清晨，敌军在日军空军支援下，对葫芦河发动全线攻击。当时，我们的弹药几乎耗尽，我军指挥官刘氏认为，除非进行殊死搏斗，否则我们将被敌军缴械，于是向方和谢发报请示对策。他们的回答是“冲出去”。接到命令后，我们准备开始突围。
方和谢的命令称，他们进行了全线反击。事实上，第十八师、第五师以及谢和方部下的部分部队参加了对敌军的反击，结果在3小时内，我们重新占领了大小山头（头山），并缴获了敌军约一个团的武装。
重新占领周屯山（小山）后，同志们普遍认为最好离开周屯山，无论是向北还是向南。同时，他们要求党总支将我方部队及受我方影响的部队集中起来，以便行动。我与在部队中从事政治工作的同志一起，询问党总支应采取何种措施。在拜访党总支时，我们遭到了我军指挥官（刘子丰）的反对，他表现出愤怒的态度，引起我们极大的不满。见局势不妙，党总支将我叫出房间，称刘最近非常动摇，并向我们解释了许多问题。然而，我对这种解释并不满意。
自从我们重新占领周屯山以来，我们在那里停留了一周，期间敌军每天都向我们发动攻击。方振武和谢凤城为了向南京投降，每天派遣代表前往北平，与何应钦（南京代理人）商议投降条款，而我方党总支对此问题持平静态度，等待方和谢的背叛。每天，同志们走访党总支成员，询问我们是跟随方和谢投降，还是执行独立的军事行动。党总支回答：“我们明天前往目的地。”今天，党总支的负责同志说“明天”去，到了明天又说还是“明天”。当然，党总支这种拖延政策不仅导致其在同志中失去信任，还招致不满，且无论如何都无济于事。最终，党总支和我军领导人（刘长仁同志）将追随方振武和谢凤城之后，出卖我军第十八师和第五师，向敌人投降。

page_data.en:
No. 66. Page 13.

In Shoutanshan, little propaganda work was made by us due chiefly to the oppression on the part of Tang and Tsie. Although it was difficult to make the propaganda openly, the semi-open activities of ours were not sufficient at all. The P.C. must naturally be responsible. Knowing that comrades and soldiers were anxious to leave Shoutanshan and fearing that the events would break out internally if they were dilly-dallying any longer, the members of the P.C., as well as our leading comrades responsible for the military work began to canvass Pang and Tsie for the departure for East Peiping from Shoutanshan. Pang Chen-wu advocated to march in the direction of East Lepai (Jehol) while Tsie Fen-cheng was in favor of advancing towards the Peiping-Hankow Railway with the intention of surrendering to Han Fu-chu, Chairman of the Shantung Provincial Government. Our Front Committee agreed the proposal of Tsie to go along the Peiping-Hankow railway, saying that we might to Kaoyang etc. (Central and South Hopei by utilizing the line pursued by Tsie.

At that time, the opinion of comrades at large was that "it is better to leave Shoutanshan no matter to what place we go", due to the fear the further drive by the enemy. Comrades considered we had better to discard Pang and Tsie, setting up our independent leadership, saying it is detrimental to our action that we continued to join hands with Pang and Tsie, under the following causes :-
(1) the larger numbers of the troops cause our military movement inconvenient, at the same time attracting the attention of the enemy.
(2) In case we want to carry through our tasks, they (Pang Chen-wu and Tsie Fen-cheng) will prevent us from doing so and in some cases dismiss us by force.
(3) If we go with the troops of Pang and Tsie, the masses are deemed incapable of discerning the difference of our troops from Pang and Tsie.
(4) Our forces will succeed in rushing at any place should we wander away from Pang and Tsie and establish our independent military movement.
(5) We should immediately leave Pang and Tsie, advancing in the direction of South Hopei.
(6) Had we continued not to wander away from Pang and Tsie, our forces will steadily be growing decreased as evidenced in the fact that during each war Pang and Tsie sent our forces like the 29th Division etc. to the foremost front as their main force, with the result that we had no method to replenish our forces after sustaining losses.
(7) The 8th Division is re-organized such, or, the 15th and 8th Divisions is re-organized into a flying corps under which are divided the big, middle and small units.
(8) In view of the problems being settled unsatisfactorily and because of the vacillation of comrades, comrades and soldiers and lower officers made their departure when in Shoutanshan.

The activities of our leading military comrades to leave Shoutanshan resulted in success. Then, our forces left for Tungchow from Shoutanshan. When we left our original position and went about 30 li., the enemy did not know our evacuation, continuing to fire on our original line.

When we arrived at a village of Hsueh Hsiang preparing to camp there overnight, it is imperative to warn them clearly through propaganda that they should either join the Japanese forces or be the Red Army.

Then, Pang Chen-wu told the members of the military in the hall of the primary school that he try to speak Mr. Pang Chien-nung in the office of the mayor. It is too late for us to go there. Then, Pang suddenly reported it immediately to the headquarters. The headquarters with pity announced the decision of dividing the order resulted in the temporary dissolution of
page_data.zh:
第66号。第13页。

在寿坛山，由于唐和谢的压迫，我们几乎未开展宣传工作。虽然公开进行宣传很困难，但我们半公开的活动也完全不足。前委自然要对此负责。鉴于同志和士兵们急于离开寿坛山，且担心若再拖延下去内部会发生变故，前委成员以及负责军事工作的我方主要领导同志开始游说庞和谢，主张从寿坛山撤往北平东部。庞振武主张向乐亭（热河）方向进军，而谢凤城则赞成向平汉铁路推进，意图向山东省政府主席韩复榘投降。我前线委员会同意了谢沿平汉铁路行进的提议，称我们可以利用谢所走的路线前往高阳等地（冀中及冀南）。

当时，广大同志的意见是“无论去哪里，最好离开寿坛山”，这是出于对敌人进一步进逼的恐惧。同志们认为我们最好抛弃庞和谢，建立独立的领导层，并称在以下原因下继续与庞和谢联手对我们的行动有害：
(1) 部队人数众多导致我军行动不便，同时也吸引了敌人的注意。
(2) 如果我们要执行任务，他们（庞振武和谢凤城）会阻止我们，甚至在某些情况下强行解散我们。
(3) 如果我们跟随庞和谢的部队，群众被认为无法分辨我军与庞、谢部队的区别。
(4) 如果我们脱离庞和谢并建立独立的军事行动，我军将能成功突袭任何地方。
(5) 我们应立即离开庞和谢，向冀南方向推进。
(6) 如果我们继续不脱离庞和谢，我军兵力将稳步减少，事实表明在每次战斗中，庞和谢都将我军如第29师等作为主力派往最前线，导致我们在遭受损失后无法补充兵力。
(7) 第8师进行了重组，或者说，第15和第8师被重组为一个飞行军团，其下分为大、中、小单位。
(8) 鉴于问题未能得到满意解决，且由于同志们的动摇，同志、士兵和下级军官在寿坛山时便已离去。

我方主要军事同志离开寿坛山的活动取得了成功。随后，我军从寿坛山前往通州。当我们离开原阵地行进约30里时，敌人并不知道我们已撤离，继续向我们原来的防线开火。

当我们到达薛乡的一个村庄准备在此过夜时，必须通过宣传明确警告他们，要么加入日军，要么加入红军。

随后，庞振武在小学礼堂告诉军方人员，他试图在市长办公室与庞剑农先生谈话。我们去那里已经太晚了。随后，庞突然立即向总部报告。总部带着怜悯宣布了一项分割命令的决定，导致部队在距离顺义县约5里的一个村庄暂时解散，以讨论后续方法。

page_data.en:
the troops in a village about 5 li far from Shueni Hsien for the discussion of the further methods.

In fact, as the bottom of this stream is sand, some parts are deep but some parts are not deep for us to pass. But Fang did not know about it.
When we arrived at Shankazen, the enemies in the city of Shueni Hsien still did not know our presence, mistaking us for their own men to be sent to fight us, and therefore they conveyed the war-supplies like about 70,000 rounds of ammunition etc. in about 10 carriages to the front in reinforcing their men. Taking this opportunity, we captured all of their war supplies.
After the arrival at Shankasen, comrades proposed not to stay there any longer, saying that we should shortly devise means and ways to cross this stream and that if not able to cross this stream we should directly rush towards the vicinities of Peiping where the enemies must be not well prepared because they are focussing their attention on Shoutanshan and Kaolocyen. Our leading military comrades and the P.C. said that "we should not run the risk;"
Until at 4 o'clock in the afternoon, the enemies launched the counter-attack on us. The 3rd Division of Tsie Pen-chong was first engaged in resisting the enemies but not an hour passed the 3rd Division was defeated with great losses. No sooner had the 3rd Division retreated than the enemy troops began fighting our 5th Division. By that time, the soldiers of the 5th Division wavered. We sent a section of the 18th Division in re-enforcing the 5th Division, instructing the 5th Division that it should not retreat whatsoever. As a result, this village was not captured by the enemies. But, the Japanese air forces continued to drop bombs into our positions, causing us to find no villages to camouflage our forces.
In the night, what measure we should take was discussed without result. Some proposed to rush out with the best of our abilities, and some suggested that we device our method until to-morrow while our Front Committee contended that to rush out is dangerous. For this reason, no troop movement was made in the night. During this time, comrades and soldiers were so vacillating that many of them made at night their desertion which is much great in contrast with that made in Shoutanshan.
In the early morning of the following day, although the Nanking troops, making the second battle against us, were repulsed by us, the Japanese sent the airplanes by longer batches to fight us from the air attack. During this engagement, garrisoning great many of houses were killed by the Japanese bombs and though the men killed were not in great number but the minds of soldiers, officers and comrades were filled with consternation. Knowing that there is no way out, all of leaders were decided to rush out at night. In the middle night, all of our forces fought the desperate battles against the enemies, with the result that the enemies were defeated and the encircled places and positions were wrested from the enemies. As soon as the day was just dawning, the Nanking troops launched a counter-attack, fighting us with machine guns, cannons, etc., but no great casualties were made on our side. The Japanese airplanes alone played the most important role in attacking us and all the villages where we were stationed were completely bombarded. We were always pursued by the Japanese forces when we escaped from villages to villages. Under the menace of the Japanese forces, it was absolutely impossible for us to escape to the hills. By that time, to sure, not only were soldiers and lower officers showing panic strickenness, but even higher officers and Tse-Pen-chong manifested vacillation.
page_data.zh:
事实上，由于这条河的底部是沙子，有些地方深，有些地方不深，足以让我们通过。但方并不知道这一点。
当我们到达善各庄时，顺义县城内的敌人仍然不知道我们的存在，误以为我们是他们派来与我们作战的自己人，因此他们用大约10辆马车向前线运送了约7万发子弹等战争物资，以增援其部队。借此机会，我们缴获了他们所有的战争物资。
到达善各庄后，同志们提议不再停留，称我们应该尽快设法渡过这条河，如果无法渡河，我们应该直接冲向北平附近，因为敌人肯定准备不足，因为他们正将注意力集中在寿坛山和高洛店。我方主要军事同志和前委表示“我们不应冒险”；
直到下午4点，敌人才对我们发动反击。谢本忠的第3师首先投入抵抗敌人，但不到一个小时，第3师就遭受重大损失而战败。第3师刚一撤退，敌军就开始与我军第5师交战。那时，第5师的士兵动摇了。我们派遣第18师的一个连去增援第5师，指示第5师无论如何不得撤退。结果，这个村庄没有被敌人攻占。但是，日本空军继续向我们的阵地投掷炸弹，导致我们找不到村庄来掩护部队。

夜间，我们讨论了应采取的措施，但没有结果。有些人提议尽力突围，有些人建议我们等到明天再想办法，而我前线委员会坚持认为突围是危险的。因此，夜间没有进行部队调动。在此期间，同志和士兵们非常动摇，许多人在夜间逃亡，这与在寿坛山时的逃亡情况相比要多得多。

第二天清晨，虽然南京部队对我们发动的第二次进攻被我们击退，但日本人派出更多批次的飞机从空中攻击我们。在这次交战中，驻守在许多房屋里的人被日本炸弹炸死，虽然死亡人数不多，但士兵、军官和同志们的内心充满了惊恐。知道已无路可退，所有领导人都决定在夜间突围。半夜，我军全体与敌人进行了殊死搏斗，结果击败了敌人，并从敌人手中夺回了被包围的地方和阵地。天刚亮，南京部队发动反击，用机枪、大炮等与我们交战，但我方伤亡不大。只有日本飞机在攻击我们方面发挥了最重要的作用，我们驻扎的所有村庄都被彻底轰炸。当我们从一个村庄逃到另一个村庄时，始终受到日军的追击。在日军的威胁下，我们绝对不可能逃入山区。那时，可以肯定的是，不仅士兵和下级军官表现出惊慌失措，甚至高级军官和谢本忠也表现出动摇。

page_data.en:
Vol. 23.    Page 12.
having no alternative to cope with the situation, desiring
nothing short of finding a way to cause them to escape to the
safe place.
At that time Fang and Tsie had made up their mind to
surrender and sent their representatives to Song Chang
(agent of Yen Shih Shan), promising to lay down their arms.
In the afternoon, they succeeded in capitulating to Nanking
and then left the troops for the headquarter of Song Cheng
who promised to send them by motorcar to the place where we
don't know. Our forces were ordered to be stationed in the
appointed places where the enemy troops surrounded us with
machine guns.
Hsu Chuan Ching was instructed by the F.C. to leave the
force. I also left the troops. It was said that our forces
would be re-organized and our army commander (Liu) would be
appointed as colonel. I considered that the enemy will force
us to lay down arms while the F.C. deemed it possible to
re-organize our force by Nanking. In the evening, an instruct-
ion came to our hands from the enemy, ordering us to lay
down arms. Otherwise, we are settled by force. After
disarmed by the enemy, comrades, the F.C. members, and sections
of soldiers went their respective way.
During the period of the disarmament by the enemy, soldiers
shed tears, saying that "we (the anti-Japanese forces) are
disarmed by the Chinese troops."
The main causes for this failure, I consider, are the
following:-
1. The Front Committee did not play the important role in
its leadership, failing to penetrate its political influence
into the mass of soldiers and instead limiting its activities
to the circles of officers and commanders.
2. The Front Committee failed to appraise the whole of the
work, never carrying on its organizational work, especially
in the forces under Fang Chen-wu and Tsie Fen-chong.
3. The work done among soldiers of the 18th and 5th Divisions
was still insufficient. The Soldiers' Committee could not
play a leading and important role, failing to discuss the
opinions expressed by lower mass of soldiers, and even was
dominated by the student-elements of the Special Guard Company.
4. There was lack of the prompt military action and the
vacillation was shown in each military movement.
5. We did not pay attention to the mass work when our forces
were stationed in the villages causing the masses to look
upon our forces as the bandit-units like the forces under
Tang Yu-ling. Although we led the poor people to conduct
the food-dividing struggles, we committed a number of mistakes
in them.
6. Each action lacked the pre-arranged plan and then there was
no method in the course of the action.
7. This failure was a result of the leadership of the right
opportunism. Our F.C. completely became a sort of a tail of
militarist.
8) The F.C. had no determination to carry out the decision
of the C.C. to prepare to go to South Hopei where we had
better work. We (lower comrades) agreed to the proposal of
the C.C.
9) The departure of Comrade Hsiaohao for Peiping caused concern
of comrades who further vacillated.

No. Jan. 20, 1934.
page_data.zh:
第23卷。第12页。
别无他法应对局势，只想找到一条路让他们逃到
安全的地方。
当时，方和谢已下定决心投降，并派遣代表去见宋长
（阎锡山的代理人），承诺放下武器。
下午，他们成功向南京方面投降，随后离开部队前往宋成
的总部，宋成承诺用汽车将他们送到一个我们
不知道的地方。我军奉命驻扎在指定地点，敌军用
机枪包围了我们。
徐传经受前线委员会指示离开部队。我也离开了部队。据说我军
将被重组，我军指挥官（刘）将被任命为上校。我认为敌人将强迫
我们放下武器，而前线委员会则认为南京方面有可能
重组我军。傍晚，我们收到了来自敌人的指令，命令我们放下
武器。否则，将以武力解决。在被敌人解除武装后，同志、前委成员和部分
士兵各自散去。
在被敌人解除武装期间，士兵们流着泪说：“我们（抗日部队）
被中国军队解除了武装。”
我认为这次失败的主要原因如下：
1. 前线委员会在其领导工作中未发挥重要作用，未能将其政治影响
渗透到广大士兵中，而是将其活动局限在军官和指挥官的圈子里。
2. 前线委员会未能评估整体工作，从未开展组织工作，特别是在
方振武和谢凤城麾下的部队中。
3. 在第18和第5师士兵中进行的工作仍然不足。士兵委员会未能
发挥领导和重要作用，未能讨论下层士兵群众表达的意见，甚至
被特务连的学生分子所主导。
4. 缺乏迅速的军事行动，且在每次军事行动中都表现出动摇。
5. 当我军驻扎在村庄时，我们没有注意群众工作，导致群众将我
军视为像唐玉麟部队那样的匪帮。虽然我们领导穷人进行分粮斗争，
但我们在其中犯了许多错误。
6. 每次行动都缺乏预先安排的计划，因此在行动过程中没有章法。
7. 这次失败是右倾机会主义领导的结果。我们的前委完全变成了
军阀的尾巴。
8) 前委没有决心执行中央委员会关于准备前往我们最好开展工作的
冀南地区的决定。我们（下级同志）同意中央委员会的提议。
9) 小豪同志前往北平引起了同志们的担忧，使他们进一步动摇。

编号：1934年1月20日。

How will the Party Branches in villages
carry out their activities?

It is worthy of discussion as to how the Party will
promote and develop the activities of Party Branches in
villages. Our decisions can be reached by studying the
following points:-

(1) Secret work in villages is absolutely impossible as
the farmers in one village are always familiar with
one another and are always ready to disclose our secrets.
(2) If we desire to carry on secret work in safety by
limiting our activities to a considerable degree, we
practically close our door against the farmer.

In view of the above we are of the opinion that
although we desire to keep to ourselves the secrets of
the Party in connection with activites in villages, we must
at the same time conduct mass movements among farmers openly
and undauntedly. We must have a clear conception of the
above points and bear them in mind for they concern greatly
the future of our revolution.

Our duties and policies in peasant movements

1) Lead the peasant masses in their daily struggles and
develop the struggles to land revolution and social
revolution.

2) Unite the poor peasants and middle class peasants and urge
them to oppose rich farmers, landlords, and the gentry.

3) Arm the peasants and induce them to carry out guerrilla
warfare against reactionary elements.

4) Hired peasants and poor peasants should be made the basis
of the party in villages.

5) Rich farmers and landlords should never be allowed to
participate in Party activities or mix with poor peasants.

6) The activities of the Party in villages should be subordinate
to the military command and the Party committees of
the peasants.

农村党支部将如何开展活动？

党如何促进和发展农村党支部的活动，值得讨论。我们可以通过研究以下几点来作出决定：-

(1) 在农村进行秘密工作绝对不可能，因为一个村的农民彼此总是很熟悉，并且随时准备泄露我们的秘密。
(2) 如果我们希望通过在很大程度上限制我们的活动来安全地进行秘密工作，我们实际上就把农民拒之门外。

鉴于上述情况，我们认为，虽然我们希望保守党在农村活动方面的秘密，但我们必须同时公开且无畏地在农民中开展群众运动。我们必须对上述几点有清晰的认识并牢记在心，因为它们关系到我们革命的未来。

我们在农民运动中的职责和政策

1) 领导农民群众进行日常斗争，并将斗争发展为土地革命和社会革命。

2) 团结贫农和中农，敦促他们反对富农、地主和士绅。

3) 武装农民，诱导他们对反动分子开展游击战。

4) 雇农和贫农应成为农村党的基础。

5) 绝不允许富农和地主参与党的活动或与贫农混在一起。

6) 党在农村的活动应服从军事指挥和农民委员会的领导。

TRANSLATION OF EXHIBIT NO. 98 SEIZED AT NO. 677 CHANGCHUN
ROAD ON MARCH 2, 1932.

A letter sent by the Central Organ to its various
branches in Manchuria and the whole body of members in
connection with the condition at that place and the work
of the Communist Party.

Since the occupation of Manchuria, the Japanese
imperialists have laid bare their ambition to interfere
with the Chinese revolution by force as a preliminary step
towards the attack upon the Soviet Russia. They are
endeavouring to colonize this large tract of land, but their
efforts do not show any great success. The economic condition
in Manchuria goes from bad to worse. Numerous exhorbitant
taxes have been imposed and the farmers have been ruthlessly
deprived of their holdings. In consequence of this terrorism,
the labourers, farmers and the bourgeoisie in Manchuria are
hostile towards the invaders and their running dogs. Meanwhile,
a revolutionary movement is being started by the labourers and
farmers in Japan against their militarist government. It seems
that the Japanese jingoists are now confronted with opposition
from within and without, but they still have aims on North
China, made possible by the non-resistance policy adopted by
the unscrupulous Kuomintang.

The Nanking Government has exposed to the public her
weakness in resisting the Japanese imperialists. The only
hope to defeat the invaders depends upon the masses. All
the volunteer leaders in Manchuria who were either under the
leadership of Chang Hsueh Liang or the direction of the
Kuomintang disappeared following the attack by the Japanese,
but the anti-imperialist movement motivated by the labourers
and farmers goes forward with increasing momentum. These
warriors are the members of the "Red Guerilla Corps" directed
by the Communist Party. They are the real revolutionists
who wish to fight for the freedom of the masses. It is,
however, a pity that the "Red Guerilla Corps" have not yet
become the leaders of the anti-Japanese movement, despite the
weight of their political influence.

The Kuomintang maintains the policy of capitulation
to the Imperialists. Taking advantage of the anti-Japanese
movement, it intensifies its attack upon the Chinese labourers
and soviet areas. Revolutionary intelligentsia and farmers
and the soldiers are being oppressed on the plea of maintaining
good order in the areas wrested from the Red Forces. The
Kuomintang assists the invaders to suppress the activities of
those who are participating in the real anti-Japanese
campaigns with iron and blood. This is evidenced in the
attitude of various cliques in the Kuomintang towards the
Manchuria problem. However each clique has its supporters.
For instance, the Nanking Clique with Chiang Kai Shek as its
leader attempted to enter into direct negotiations with the
Japanese Imperialists and promised to comply with the
demands of the "puppet" regime of Mukden. Meanwhile
it makes a show of opposing the Japanese invasion of Manchuria
with the object of obtaining the aid of the American
Imperialists. The Canton Clique supports the neutrality
of China regarding the Sino-Japanese conflict in
Manchuria. The Western Hills Clique advocates that
the power should be vested in the hands of the military leaders
so that the British Imperialists would be able to put forth
their plan to occupy the two provinces in question.

中央机关就当地情况及共产党工作致满洲各支部及全体会员的一封信。

自从满洲被占领以来，日本帝国主义者暴露了他们以武力干涉中国革命的野心，这是进攻苏俄的初步步骤。他们正努力殖民这片广阔的土地，但他们的努力并未显示出任何巨大的成功。满洲的经济状况每况愈下。征收了无数苛捐杂税，农民被无情地剥夺了土地。由于这种恐怖统治，满洲的工人、农民和资产阶级对侵略者及其走狗充满敌意。与此同时，日本的工人和农民正在发起反对军国主义政府的革命运动。看来日本沙文主义者现在面临着内外 opposition，但他们仍然觊觎华北，这得以实现是因为无耻的国民党采取了不抵抗政策。

南京政府向公众暴露了其在抵抗日本帝国主义者方面的软弱。击败侵略者的唯一希望在于民众。满洲所有曾在张学良领导下或受国民党指挥的义勇军领袖，在日本进攻后都消失了，但由工人和农民推动的反帝运动正以日益增长的势头向前发展。这些战士是由共产党领导的“红色游击队”的成员。他们是真正的革命者，希望为群众的自由而战。然而，遗憾的是，“红色游击队”尽管具有政治影响力，但尚未成为抗日运动的领导者。

国民党维持着向帝国主义者投降的政策。它利用抗日运动，加紧对中国工人和苏区的攻击。以在从红军手中夺回的地区维持良好秩序为借口，压迫革命知识分子、农民和士兵。国民党协助侵略者用铁腕和血腥手段镇压那些参与真正抗日 campaign 的人的活动。国民党各派系对满洲问题的态度证明了这一点。然而，每个派系都有其支持者。例如，以蒋介石为首的南京派试图与日本帝国主义者进行直接谈判，并承诺遵守沈阳“傀儡”政权的要求。同时，它假装反对日本入侵满洲，目的是获得美国帝国主义者的援助。广东派支持中国在满洲中日冲突中保持中立。西山派主张权力应掌握在军事领导人手中，以便英国帝国主义者能够提出占领这两个相关省份的计划。

page_data.en:
Exhibit No.35. Page 2.

The above facts show that only the Communist
International and the Central Organ maintain a reasonable
attitude towards the Manchuria Problem. They aim at the
overthrow of the reactionary National Government and intend
to lead the armed masses to carry on the national revolution
and anti-Imperialist warfare in order to maintain Chinese
independence. With a view to avoiding failure, we should
make every effort to stabilize our party influence in
Manchuria and fight for the leadership in the anti-Japanese
movement as well as other "People's Activities".

We should try not only to effect the emancipation
of our race and to protect "Soviet" China, but also to
accomplish our international duty, that is to support
Soviet Russia by force of arms.

In order to reach this goal, we must first
of all show and maintain a united front to beat down the
running dogs and the Japanese Imperialists, and pave the way
to our victory in Manchuria. The following points should be
borne in mind when executing our plan :-

(1) To maintain our political independence, i.e. to keep
close watch on the intrigues of rebels, and to oppose
the "Rightist Elements" and deprive of the leadership
of proletarian class.
/thm

(2) To pay close attention to the conditions when we
execute our plan. Remember always that our activities
should start among the soldiers and volunteers to form
a strong united front in the anti-Japanese campaign.

(3) To accelerate the political education and organizing
power of the proletarian class so that they will be
able to extend their struggle for their political and
economic benefit.

The proletarian class in Manchuria, both in number
or in quality, are the greatest political power. They have
frequently declared strikes and participated in guerrilla
warfare, which shows that they are fundamental force of the
people's revolutionary war front. However, their
activities still require the direction of our party.
We should therefore assist them in demanding better
treatment from their employers and show opposition to
the closing down of concerns whereby they are thrown out
of employment.
page_data.zh:
证物第35号。第2页。

上述事实表明，只有共产国际和中央机关对满洲问题保持着理性的态度。他们的目标是推翻反动的国民政府，并意图领导武装群众进行民族革命和反帝战争，以维护中国的独立。为了避免失败，我们应竭尽全力稳定我党在满洲的影响力，争取在抗日运动及其他“民众活动”中的领导权。

我们不仅要致力于本民族的解放和保护“苏维埃”中国，还要履行我们的国际义务，即以武力支援苏俄。

为了达到这一目标，我们必须首先展示并维持统一战线，以打击走狗和日本帝国主义者，为我们在满洲的胜利铺平道路。在执行我们的计划时，应牢记以下几点：-

(1) 保持我们的政治独立性，即密切监视叛徒的阴谋，反对“右派分子”，并剥夺其对无产阶级阶级的领导权。
/thm

(2) 在执行计划时密切关注局势。始终记住，我们的活动应从士兵和志愿者中开始，以在抗日运动中形成强大的统一战线。

(3) 加速无产阶级阶级的政治教育和组织能力，使他们能够扩展其为政治和经济利益而进行的斗争。

满洲的无产阶级阶级，无论在数量还是质量上，都是最大的政治力量。他们经常举行罢工并参与游击战，这表明他们是人民革命战争战线的基本力量。然而，他们的活动仍然需要我党的指导。因此，我们应该协助他们向雇主争取更好的待遇，并反对导致他们失业的企业关闭行为。

General Principles of activities of Industrial Branches.

1) To ascertain the following particulars about factories:-
Capital, nationality, business conditions, treatment
of workers, wages, number of workers, their sex and
native places. Oppression of workers by capitalists
and foremen; Factory regulations; strikes and their
results; labour unions; picketing parties or boys
groups; sufferings of workers and demands.

2) Particulars of communist branches in factories: their
activities in the past and present.

3) Organization of Branches: membership, cells, number
of female party members.

4) Meetings of Branches: whether the meetings are held
within or without the factory and whether the meetings
are held regularly.

5) Direction of struggles: views of comrades relating to
struggles; do the Branches discuss and prepare for
struggles? Do the Branches endeavour to start
strikes? Are there strike committees? How to
deal with traitors. How to oppose in strikes
mediation by the Bureau of Social Affairs.

6) Anti-Japanese movement: The effects of the Manchurian
incident on workers. The Anti-Japanese feelings of
workers. Have the Branches conducted anti-Japanese
movement openly in factories? Have the Branches
done anything in the form of anti-Japanese demonstrations?
Have the Branches established volunteer armies and
storming parties?

7) Particulars of activities against Yellow Labour Unions
and their leaders.

8) Propaganda work and training of workers.

9) Particulars of the enlisting of new comrades by the
Branches in factories.

10) Particulars of Branches of Youth Leagues in factories.
Do the Party Branches direct their activities?

工业支部活动总则。

1) 查明工厂的以下详情：资本、国籍、经营状况、工人待遇、工资、工人人数、性别及籍贯。资本家和工头对工人的压迫；工厂规章；罢工及其结果；工会；纠察队或童子军团体；工人的苦难与诉求。

2) 工厂内共产党支部的详情：其过去和现在的活动。

3) 支部的组织：党员人数、细胞小组、女党员人数。

4) 支部会议：会议是在工厂内部还是外部举行，以及会议是否定期举行。

5) 斗争的指导：同志们在斗争方面的观点；支部是否讨论并为斗争做准备？支部是否努力发动罢工？是否有罢工委员会？如何处理叛徒。如何在罢工中反对社会局的调解。

6) 抗日运动：满洲事变对工人的影响。工人的抗日情绪。支部是否在工厂内公开开展抗日运动？支部是否进行过任何形式的抗日示威？支部是否建立了义勇军和突击队？

7) 反对黄色工会及其领导人的活动详情。

8) 宣传工作和工人培训。

9) 工厂支部招募新同志的详情。

10) 工厂内青年团支部的详情。党支部是否指导他们的活动？

Translation of Exhibit No 96.

Particulars of the 6th Route North-Eastern Volunteer Army:-

Commander.
Graduate from the Military Academy in Japan. He has held the
following positions:- Battalion Commander, Regimental
Commander and Commander of the North-Eastern Student Corps.

Officers.
Commanding officers are mostly students of the former Military
Academy in the North-east. The junior officers are mostly
teachers, students and ex-soldiers.

Strength.
Infantry, Artillery, Cavalry and Machine Gun Corps, totalling
4.740 men. 500 horses.
Armament.
Eight Stokes Guns. 13 Machine Guns. 3.400 rifles.

Daily life of Soldiers.
Apart from attending lectures and undergoing military training
they assist the people in farming, in repairing or building
roads, as a consequence of which they are welcomed by the farmers
and proletarian classes, but the landlords do not sympathise
with them.

Financial Resources.
Formerly the army received some financial support from the
People's Support Committee but it stopped sending money
following the signing of the Peace Pact in North China. At
present, the Army is being supported by the private income of
the Commander.

Attitude of the Army towards
the National Government.
The men of the Army are mostly natives of the North East. They
are opposed to the non-resistance policy of the National
Government. Moreover the Government does not support them but
disarms the Volunteer Armies whenever opportunity presents itself.
As a consequence of the attitude of the Government
this army is not on good terms with XXXXXXXXXXXX the
National Government.

东北义勇军第六路军详情：-

指挥官。
毕业于日本陆军士官学校。他曾担任以下职务：营长、团长及东北学生军团指挥官。

军官。
指挥官多为前东北陆军士官学校的学生。下级军官多为教师、学生和退伍士兵。

兵力。
步兵、炮兵、骑兵和机枪连，共计4,740人。马匹500匹。
武器。
斯托克斯迫击炮8门。机枪13挺。步枪3,400支。

士兵的日常生活。
除了听课和接受军事训练外，他们还帮助百姓耕种、修路或筑路，因此受到农民和无产阶级阶级的欢迎，但地主不同情他们。

财政来源。
此前，该军队从民众支援委员会获得了一些财政支持，但在华北和平协定签署后，该委员会停止汇款。目前，该军队由指挥官的个人收入供养。

军队对国民政府的态度。
该军队士兵多为东北人。他们反对国民政府的不抵抗政策。此外，政府不支持他们，反而一有机会就解除义勇军的武装。由于政府的这种态度，这支军队与XXXXXXXXXXXX国民政府关系不佳。

Condition in Kiangsi

Nan-cheng, Jan. 5.

Number of troops in Eastern Kiangsi

Wu-chow - a portion of 13th Division.
Nan-cheng - a portion of 98th Division.
Nan-foong - 8th Division.
Siao-suh - 145th Regiment of the 24th Division.
The 2nd Battalion of this Regiment are
undertaking the construction of roads
and fortifications between Siao-suh
and Lee Chuan.
Hung-men - 139th Regiment.
Ts Chi Jao - 143rd Regiment.
Loh Yah; Fee Et; and Ping Kwan - 144th Regiment.
Lee Chuan - a portion of the 6th Division.
Chung Yen - 96th Division.
Tuan Chen - 5th Division.
Sing Kow : 11th and 67th Divisions.
Fee Et - 94th Division.
Kwang Shih - 87th and 89th Divisions.
Hu Fang - 36th Divisions.

The military Headquarters previously at
Nan-cheng is now at Shan-yue. General Chen Sheng is
at Lee Chuan but is reported to be leaving soon for
Fokien. According to an unconfirmed report, General
Sih Yah will be promoted Commander-in-Chief of the
Northern Route Army.

Fortifications.

White armies regard the building of fortifications
as their most important task. Whenever they occupy a
place they build fortifications at important strategic
points. Consequently many fortifications have been
built along the way route from Fuchow, Lee Chuan, Nancheng,
to TshDung Kwan. Owing to the mountainous nature of
the country only cannons and/or airplanes would be able
to launch an effective attack upon them. White armies
are in the habit of pulling down people's houses in
order to obtain materials for building fortifications.
A number of people have returned to the areas occupied
by the white soldiers and are indignant at the destruction
caused by them. Many of those who have returned to
their homes have been killed by White armies on the
grounds that they were spies of Red Armies.

The 1st Battalion of the 1st Artillery Regiment with
18 field guns, left Nanking for Wuchow (Canton) on Jan. 12.
The 2nd Battalion left Nanking for Foochow via Shanghai
about two weeks ago visited the Government Arsenal there
and transported Guns shipped to Shanghai via Wusung on
January 10, arriving at Shanghai on 14th.

原驻南城的军事总部现已迁至山岳（音译）。陈胜将军在李川（音译），但据报道他即将前往福建。据未经证实的消息，司亚（音译）将军将被提升为北路军总司令。

工事。

白军将修筑工事视为其最重要的任务。每当他们占领一个地方，就会在重要的战略要点修筑工事。因此，从福州、李川（音译）、南城到赤东关（音译，原文不清）的沿途修建了许多工事。由于该地区多山，只有大炮和/或飞机才能对其发动有效攻击。白军习惯拆毁民房以获取修筑工事的材料。许多人回到了被白军占领的地区，并对他们造成的破坏感到愤怒。许多返回家园的人被白军以红军间谍为由杀害。

炮兵第一团第一营携18门野战炮，于1月12日离开南京前往梧州（广州）。第二营约两周前离开南京经上海前往福州，参观了那里的政府兵工厂，并运输了1月10日经吴淞运抵上海的枪支，于14日抵达上海。

The Cantonese troops in Southern Kiangsi have been
withdrawn to the borders of Kwangtung, whilst Kungchow
(Kiangsi) has been taken over by General Ho Chien's troops.

The troops of Bau Kong have been transferred from
u-seng-kwan to the u-zang Line.

Nanchang

According to people coming from Nanchang, when the
Red Armies occupied Sung Mei Tsung and advanced upon
Nanchang, gunfire was audible within the city of Nanchang
and the people were greatly excited. The Bogus Military
Headquarters at Nanchang immediately issued a proclamation
stating that the gunfire was a target practice and that
the people should not allow themselves to become excited.
Military spies were very active, it was only necessary to
speak of the Red Army to be arrested and executed.

南昌

据从南昌来的人说，当红军占领宋梅宗（音译）并向南昌推进时，南昌城内可听到枪声，民众极为激动。南昌的伪军事总部立即发布公告，称枪声是实弹演习，民众不应惊慌。军事间谍非常活跃，只要提及红军就会被逮捕并处决。

A letter to Huhfei (合肥) Hsien Committee

According to a report from the inspectors, the Central
considers that the work of the Huhfei Party (Anhwei) is
quite strong. Despite several attacks from the outside
you have been able to strengthen the organization.

The above result is, however, still insufficient, the
following defects are brought to your notice :-

1. The Huhfei Party and the masses are far apart. As the
work has not yet penetrated deep into the masses, only
a few of them participated in struggles conducted by
your party. Furthermore, you do not carry out our
work among labourers and soldiers in the locality.
You have to break down these obstacles, otherwise
developments will be retarded.

2. There are also many errors in the policy and preparations
for conducting struggles. You make no proper preparations
before establishment and do not follow up the success
obtained with a propaganda campaign, as a consequence you
are unable to enlarge the scale of the movement and direct
the struggle for greater objectives.

3. You must work daily to establish mass organizations.
Although a "peasants committee" has been formed in
the Huhfei Hsien, it does no practical work.

4. You have done no work among soldiers and workers in
your city. No plan for carrying out such work has yet
been formulated by you. You moreover don't know how to
conduct anti-Kuomintang and anti-Imperialist struggles nor
how to support the Soviet.

5. The Hsien Committee has no practical power in holding
meetings, directing the work of sub-committees and mass
organizations. With the exception of the Su Sung (City)
Special District Sub-Committee, the district under the
Huhfei Hsien show no appreciable development in activities.
At present there are not more than 60 members in the Hsien
Committee. This number is much smaller than before.

The Huhfei Hsien Committee up to the present time has
not progressed satisfactorily. Now with a view to extending
your activities in the future we give you the following
instructions :-

The "Manchukuo" in North China will not minimize the
ambition of the Japanese Imperialists in invading China. The
"Anti-Red District" in Kiangsi is already in the hands of the
Japanese Imperialists, while Chiang Kai-shek is still busy
with his own internal affairs and cannot afford to
attack Sikang out of the same time invade Manchuria.
Recently the militarists in Szechuan made certain agreements
with the Japanese Imperialists, thus enabling the latter to
take not only Sikang but Szechuan as well. Meanwhile the
French Imperialists are now active in Yunnan and Kwangsi
while the Japanese have occupied 8 small islands in the
South of Kwangtung.

致合肥县委的一封信

根据视察员的报告，中央认为合肥党（安徽）的工作相当有力。尽管遭受了几次外部攻击，你们仍加强了组织。

然而，上述成果仍然不足，现提请你们注意以下缺陷：-

1. 合肥党与群众相距甚远。由于工作尚未深入群众，只有少数人参与了由你们党领导的斗争。此外，你们没有在当地工人和士兵中开展我们的工作。你们必须打破这些障碍，否则发展将会受阻。

2. 在开展斗争的政策和准备方面也存在许多错误。你们在建立之前没有做好适当的准备，也没有通过宣传运动来巩固取得的成果，因此你们无法扩大运动的规模并将斗争引向更大的目标。

3. 你们必须每天努力建立群众组织。虽然在合肥县成立了“农民委员会”，但它没有开展任何实际工作。

4. 你们没有在城市的士兵和工人中开展工作。你们尚未制定开展此类工作的计划。此外，你们不知道如何进行反国民党和反帝斗争，也不知道如何支援苏维埃。

5. 县委在召开会议、指导分委会和群众组织工作方面没有实权。除苏松（市）特别区分委会外，合肥县下属各区在活动方面均无明显发展。目前，县委成员不超过60人。这一数字比以前少得多。

迄今为止，合肥县委的进展并不令人满意。现在，为了将来扩展你们的活动，我们给予你们以下指示：-

华北的“满洲国”不会削弱日本帝国主义者侵略中国的野心。江西的“防共区”已经落入日本帝国主义者手中，而蒋介石正忙于其内部事务，无暇同时进攻西康并入侵满洲。最近，四川的军阀与日本帝国主义者达成某些协议，从而使后者不仅能夺取西康，还能夺取四川。与此同时，法国帝国主义者目前在云南和广西活动，而日本人已占领了广东南部的8个小岛。

TRANSLATION OF EXHIBIT NO. 104 SEIZED DURING THE COURSE
OF A RAID AT NO. 677 CHAOPEING ROAD ON MARCH 2, 1934.

A.

At 2 p.m. on the 22nd the executive staff of the
Section and the District Committee held a meeting to
discuss the following problems :-
Opposition to the 5th Anti-Communist Campaign,
Organization of Red Army Friendly Societies,
Anti-Imperialist Activities.
I did not participate in this meeting as I went to
see the Clerk of the Section who, however, was absent.

Methods of propaganda: I suggest that comrades
should meet workers outside factories at the time of going
to or leaving work and talk with them about their treatment
and living conditions, secure their addresses and induce
them to join the party.
A factory newspaper was once issued and a copy was
posted in the factory but was torn up by reactionaries.
As newspapers form an important propaganda medium, further
issues should be published.
About one hundred copies of the "Labourers' Newspaper"
of the Labour Federation were disseminated in factories.
Some male workers picked them up and read them.

B.

At 6 p.m. October 8, I interviewed the Clerk of the
District Committee who gave me the following information:-
The Anti-Imperialist League consists of the
following 18 comrades who are all natives of Hunan :-
Weaving Room workers.....7
Cotton Yarn Room Workers.8
Cotton Pasting Room " 2
Hot Water Room " 1
The factory has a complement of 3,000 workers of
whom 300 are females. The Clerk of the Branch in the
factory is not sufficiently energetic in his work and the
Branch has failed to carry out the following duties:-
A movement to support the strike of Shanghai Power Co.
Workers and organizing of parties to comfort strikers
and dog-beating parties.

------------------

I went to see him again on the 9th but I had no
chance to talk with him as three of his friends came to
play Mahjong with him. When I went to see him on the 11th,

I understand that he fears dismissal from the factory
should I visit him too often.

C.

1. Social Scientists: at least 5 men.
2. Students: as many as possible.
3. Absorb as many assistants of high class shops as possible.
4. Absorb five comrade from amongst industrial workers.

D.

Letters to members of Publication Dept. and Printing Dept.
Our comrades are conducting their own individual campaigns
in a feverish manner. Now is the time for expansion and success

A.

22日下午2时，该科执行人员与区委员会举行会议，讨论以下问题：
反对第五次“剿共”运动，
组织红军之友社，
反帝活动。
我未参加此次会议，因我去见该科书记员，但他不在。

宣传方法：我建议同志们在工人上下班时在工厂外与他们会面，谈论他们的待遇和生活状况，获取他们的地址并诱导他们入党。
曾发行过一份厂报，并将一份张贴在工厂内，但被反动分子撕毁。鉴于报纸是重要的宣传媒介，应继续出版。
劳工联合会的《劳工报》约有一百份在工厂内散发。一些男工捡起阅读。

B.

10月8日下午6时，我会见了区委员会书记员，他向我提供了以下信息：
反帝联盟由以下18名同志组成，均为湖南籍：
织布间工人……7人
棉纱间工人……8人
棉浆间工人……2人

Translation of Exhibit No.165 seized at 677 Changping

Report of the Hankow Branch League of the Leftist Clique

1. Politics at Hankow : The flood and the extension of
Soviet districts have caused a general slump in business,
while the oppression of the Imperialists has driven
industry to a road of ruin.

It is safe to say that the political stage at Hankow
is made up of loafers and professional corrupt officials.
These are "indirect" running dogs of Imperialists and
"direct" running dogs of the Nanking Government. Apart
from struggling for personal benefits, they take the
suppression of revolutionary movements as their main object.

Owing to the extent of farming villages becoming
smaller and smaller, they can not help accelerate exploitation
of the masses. In other words, they create a number of
levies (such as signboard tax, business tax, etc. in
farming villages). They furthermore propose the formation
of model villages or districts so as to complete their
exploitation of the masses.

It is a fact that cotton mills reduced working hours
and finally suspended operations. It cannot be denied
that it is a heavy blow to the proletariat. However, it
can also be said that their revolutionary strength has been
augmented thereby. This can be evidenced by the
declaration of strikes and putting forth of demands on the
part of labourers. These events are published widely in
the press.

Armed soldiers and detectives are posted in the
vicinity of industrial concerns, which preserves "good"
order among the labourers. However, the papers tell us
that the labourers are silenced and oppressed.

Not only is the movement of the proletariat limited,
but the mouth of the intellectuals who are in sympathy with
the proletariat is closed. They want to separate the
intellectuals and students from the present society.
By such means, they are in a position to monopolize
education.

Fascist followers, needless to say, have been posted
among teachers and students as spies. The students are
given a large amount of work to do (such as military
training during the summer vacation, etc) so that they are
unable to spare time for other enterprises.

So-called News, Postal Matter and Telegram Censorship
Committees are formed to suppress the journalists, etc.

1934年3月2日在昌平路677号查获的证物第165号译文

左翼团体汉口支部联盟报告

1. 汉口政局：洪水及苏区的扩展导致商业普遍萧条，而帝国主义的压迫使工业走向毁灭之路。

可以说，汉口的政治舞台是由闲散人员和职业腐败官员组成的。这些人是帝国主义的“间接”走狗和南京政府的“直接”走狗。除了争夺个人利益外，他们将镇压革命运动作为主要目标。

由于农村范围越来越小，他们不得不加速对群众的剥削。换言之，他们在农村设立各种捐税（如招牌税、营业税等）。此外，他们提议建立模范村或区，以完成对群众的剥削。

棉纺厂减少工时并最终停工是事实。不可否认，这对无产阶级是一个沉重打击。然而，也可以说他们的革命力量由此增强。这可以从工人宣布罢工并提出要求得到证明。这些事件在报刊上广泛刊登。

武装士兵和侦探被部署在工业企业附近，以维持工人中的“良好”秩序。然而，报纸告诉我们，工人被噤声和压迫。

不仅无产阶级的运动受到限制，同情无产阶级的知识分子的嘴也被封住。他们希望将知识分子和学生与当前社会隔离开来。通过这种手段，他们能够垄断教育。

法西斯追随者无疑已被安插在教师和学生中充当间谍。学生被分配大量工作要做（如暑假期间的军事训练等），使他们无暇顾及其他事业。

所谓新闻、邮件和电报审查委员会成立，以压制记者等。

page_data.en:
Ex.105
-2-

2. Civilization in Hankow:

The main object of newspaper men in Hankow is to obtain some allowance. They have no knowledge of journalism and all articles are reproductions of Shanghai papers and foreign news reports. There are a large number of mosquito papers, most of which are, however, dealing with love matters.

The 3rd Department of the Four Provinces Bandit Suppression Headquarters is the organ to conduct civilization movements of a Fascist nature. The departmental chief is Tung Wen-I (鄧文儀), native of Hunan, and his assistants are named Shiang Bei-liang (向培良) and Woo Wei-feng (吳雲風), etc. Shiang Bei-liang published a magazine entitled "Youth Comment" (30,000 characters each issue), which is a Fascist periodical. It is not popular, but it continues to be published. Another man Wong Ching-li (王荊侶), a graduate of the Wihan University, published a periodical entitled "Middle School Students at Hankow" (60,000 characters each issue). It claims that 3,000 of each issue are sold, but it is hardly a fact.

They also form literary organizations to conduct spy tasks. The men undertaking such work called "civilization secret investigator". Shiang Bei-liang is one of them.

Their "masses" are opportunists and seekers of allowances.

3. Work of the Branch League in the past

We have submitted a detailed report on the events in October of last year. The following is what took place after April of this (7) year :-

a) Organization: We only have some 20 persons. As the number is small, it is impossible to subdivide ourselves into various departments. There are four sections formed according to districts. Each section has a clerk and these sections hold joint meetings. There is a general clerk and a general "communication". Under this general "communication", there is a "communication" at Yuchang and another at Hankow. They are concurrently doing "distribution" tasks.

b) Principles: Apart from "entering" into the bourgeoisie and intellectuals and establishing the case of labourers and peasants civilization the "civilization" workers are required to organize the intellectuals, labourers and peasants. These tasks which have been destroyed should be resumed forthwith.

c) Work: The only secret work is to disseminate propaganda and write slogans. The following are public activities:-
We have the translations of the 24 old plays (二十四史劇本), Hung Lou Meng (紅樓夢) and Sing King Daily News (星京日報副刊).
It is a pity that we have very few writers.
Regarding Broadcasting. Owing to lack of opportunity and funds, no theatricais were staged. Recently nothing dispensed.
page_data.zh:
证物105
-2-

2. 汉口文化：

汉口报人的主要目的是获得一些津贴。他们不懂新闻业务，所有文章都是上海报纸和外国新闻报道的翻版。有大量的小报，但大多数都涉及恋爱事务。

四省剿匪总部第三处是开展法西斯性质文化运动的机构。该处处长为邓文仪（湖南人），其助手名为向培良和吴云风等。向培良出版了一本名为《青年评论》的杂志（每期3万字），这是一本法西斯刊物。它并不受欢迎，但仍继续出版。另一人王荊侶，武汉大学毕业生，出版了一本题为《汉口中学生》的期刊（每期6万字）。它声称每期售出3000份，但这几乎不是事实。

他们还组建文学组织以执行间谍任务。从事此类工作的人被称为“文化秘密调查员”。向培良就是其中之一。

他们的“群众”是投机分子和津贴寻求者。

3. 支部联盟过去的工作

我们就去年十月份的事件提交了详细报告。以下是今年（民国）七年四月之后发生的情况：

a) 组织：我们只有约20人。由于人数少，不可能细分为各个部门。按地区成立了四个组。每组设一名书记员，这些组举行联席会议。设有一名总书记员和一名总“交通”。在该总“交通”之下，裕昌和汉口各有一名“交通”。他们同时兼任“分发”任务。

b) 原则：除了“打入”资产阶级和知识分子以及建立工农文化案例外，“文化”工作者被要求组织知识分子、工人和农民。这些已被破坏的任务应立即恢复。

c) 工作：唯一的秘密工作是散发宣传和书写标语。以下是公开活动：
我们有二十四部旧剧剧本、《红楼梦》和《星京日报副刊》的译本。
遗憾的是，我们的作家很少。
关于广播。由于缺乏机会和资金，没有上演戏剧。最近没有发布任何内容。

Books & Newspaper Society This is a place where books
are hired out. It has a membership of 70 or 80 persons.
It is one most hopeful organization, but it is not in a
position to purchase new books owing to financial difficulties.
Schools: There are some schools for children of workers.
The time before a lesson is utilized to explain to the
students the duty of labourers, the position of China, etc.
Several of the students have entered factories as workers.
We are preparing to "enter" into the labourers by this
way.

d. Latest Resolutions :
1. That the summer vacation be utilized to extend the
"organization".
2. That the summer vacation be utilized to establish
"farming village communication cells."
3. That political training of our own be accelerated.
4. That arrangements be made to publish a public
periodical and a mimeographed publication of "interior"
affairs.
5. That efforts be made to "enter" into private middle
and primary schools.

e. Difficulties
(1) Lack of directorship.
(2) Lack of books and periodicals.
(3) Lack of men able to/ work.
(4) Lack of experience in v...

4. We make the following demands from the National Literary
Federation :-
a) That the Hankow Branch League maintain "communication"
with the National Literary Federation.
b) That the Federation supply the Branch League with as
many books as possible from the point of view of
organization.
c) That the Federation compel the Branch League to have
direct relation with the Party.
d) That the Federation assign at least one member to direct
work in Hankow.
e) That the writers of the Federation contribute as many
of their writings as possible to the Branch League.
f) That a reply on the foregoing demands be given forthwith.

August 22.

学校：有一些为工人子女开设的学校。课前时间用于向学生解释工人的责任、中国的地位等。几名学生已进入工厂当工人。我们正准备通过这种方式“打入”工人之中。

5. 努力“打入”私立中学和小学。

(2) 缺乏书籍和期刊。

4. 我们向全国文学联合会提出以下要求：
a) 汉口支部联盟与全国文学联合会保持“交通”联系。
b) 联合会从组织角度尽可能向支部联盟提供书籍。
c) 联合会迫使支部联盟与党建立直接关系。
d) 联合会指派至少一名成员指导汉口的工作。
e) 联合会的作家尽可能多地向支部联盟供稿。
f) 立即对上述要求给予答复。

8月22日。

Restoration and Consolidation of
Unions of Industrial Workers.

1) Federation of Cotton Mill Workers' Unions :-
a) The Eastern District Cotton Mill Workers' Office shall
have a staff of 11 comrades (8 male and 3 female workers)
b) As we have connections in the Sung Sing No.1 Mill and
the Japan-China Cotton Mill, we can restore the Western
District Cotton Mill Workers' Office at once by means
of "storming" methods.
c) We have to consolidate the branch unions in the Heng
Foong, Hwo, Sung Sing No.6, San Sing and Shanghai No.1
Cotton Mills, and to ensure that their daily work is
duly carried out.

2) Federation of Tobacco Workers' Unions :-
a) As we have connections in the B.A.T. No.3 Factory,
Nanyang Tobacco Co., American Tobacco Co., Kiangnan,
Hwa Tung, and Hwa Ping Tobacco Companies, we can now
establish therein branch unions and red cells.
b) We should call a meeting of representatives of various
factories prior to the Anniversary of the International
Youth Day. Five persons (3 male and 2 female workers)
should be chosen to make preparations for the meeting.

3) Federation of Municipal Workers :-
a) Consolidate the Standing Committee which should consist
of five persons, two of whom should be employed at
present. (one employed in the post office and one in
the Shanghai Tramway Co,)
b) Consolidate our connections in the post offices and
the Shanghai Tramway Co., and restore our connections
with the workers of the French and Nantao tramway
companies, the bus company, and ricksha coolies.
c) Establish connections with other electricity workers
and workers of waterworks companies.

4) Federation of Metal Workers :-
a) Establish branch unions and red cells in the Zoom Tain
(造錠), Hwa Tung(華東), Sing Cheng(信昌) and Pathe
Factories wherein we have connections.
b) Prior to the Anniversary of the International Youth
Day, we should call a meeting of representatives of
the above mentioned factories. We should appoint
from 3 to 5 persons to make preparations for the
meeting (two of the persons should be employed at
present).

5) Federation of Wharf Workers :-
a) Transform the organizations at Wuchow Road, Shiuang
Yan Jae, Lee Foh Dee, Lan Hyi Dee and other places
into branch unions or red cells.
b) Before the anniversary of the International Youth Day,
we should call a meeting of representatives from various
places and establish an office of the Federation.
c) Develop the "Anti-Japanese Boycott Group" into ten groups.

6) Recover all "lost ground" such as the Federation of Printing
Workers, the Federation of Shop Assistants and the Federa-
tion of Unemployed Workers, and organize storming parties
to undertake this task. The Party and the League should
be requested to render assistance.

7) Enlist 1,000 new members on the September 18 Anniversary.

恢复与巩固产业工人工会。

1) 棉厂工人工会联合会：-
a) 东区棉厂工人办事处应配备11名同志（8名男工和3名女工）
b) 由于我们在申新第一厂和华商纱厂有联系，我们可以立即通过“突击”方法恢复西区棉厂工人办事处。
c) 我们必须巩固恒丰、厚生、申新第六厂、三新和上海第一棉厂的分支工会，并确保其日常工作得到适当开展。

2) 烟草工人工会联合会：-
a) 由于我们在英美烟草公司第三厂、南洋烟草公司、美国烟草公司、江南、华通和华平烟草公司有联系，我们现在可以在其中建立分支工会和红色细胞。
b) 我们应该在国际青年节纪念日之前召开各工厂代表会议。应选出五人（3名男工和2名女工）为会议做准备。

3) 市政工人联合会：-
a) 巩固常务委员会，该委员会应由五人组成，其中两人目前受雇。（一人在邮局工作，一人在上海电车公司工作，）
b) 巩固我们在邮局和上海电车公司的联系，并恢复我们与法商和南市电车公司、公共汽车公司以及黄包车夫的联系。
c) 与其他电力工人和水务公司工人建立联系。

4) 金属工人联合会：-
a) 在我们有联系的造錠、華東、信昌和百代工厂建立分支工会和红色细胞。
b) 在国际青年节纪念日之前，我们应该召开上述工厂的代表会议。我们应该任命3至5人为会议做准备（其中两人目前受雇）。

5) 码头工人联合会：-
a) 将梧州路、双燕记、李发记、兰义记等地的组织转变为分支工会或红色细胞。
b) 在国际青年节纪念日之前，我们应该召开各地代表会议，并设立联合会办事处。
c) 将“抵制日货小组”发展为十个小组。

6) 收复所有“失地”，如印刷工人联合会、店员联合会和失业工人联合会，并组织突击队来承担这项任务。应请求党和团提供协助。

7) 在九一八纪念日招募1,000名新成员。

A RAID CONDUCTED AT NO. 677 CHANGPING ROAD ON MARCH 2,1934

To "Central" and Central Publication Department,

I have been attached to the Central Publication
Department for a long time and my work and activities in
the past are well known to my comrades of the department.
I submit hereunder a brief report on the recent "incident"
as well as my doings after my release from jail :-

Cause of Arrest

Up to the present we are still ignorant of the cause
of our arrest. According to certain workers and my personal
conviction, it may be attributed to the following :-
(1) Information given by the chief tenant of House No. 18 Tai
Oen Li(泰安里), Shanse Road, because this individual had
quarrels with Dah Loong(大龍) on several occasions and
he knew what we were binding. He probably had some
connection with the Public Safety Bureau.
(2) Lan Woo(老吴) knew many renegades. He was not very
careful of his own movements and went very often to his
home in Dalny Road.
(3) Tseu Kwang Yen(周光言) also knew a number of renegades
of the Printing Department. The workers did not know
the secret work. For instance, one named Zung(陈),
who was arrested at the same time, was visiting House
No.18 to ask Tseu Kwang Yen to repay some money due to
him. None of the workers said anything as to how Zung
came to know House No.18.
(4) Yeong Bah(云白) and Wu Sz Ching(胡世清) knew our
Publication Department very well. As they have
surrendered to the Kuomintang it is possible that
information had been supplied by them.

Arrests following the arrest

House No.18 was raided on April 3. House No. 101
was subsequently visited and workers taken into custody.
Kwang Tung Tuh(廣東佬) was arrested at 9 a.m. April 4 at
House No.18. Lieu You Ching(刘友清) and I were arrested
at 4 p.m. April 4 at House No.57. We were subjected to
severe interrogation and torture at the police station. We
were handed over to the Public Safety Bureau on April 12.
On May 28 we were transferred to the Soochow High Court for
preliminary hearing. The case against Kwang Tung Tuh(廣東佬),
Tseu Kwang Yen(周光言) and Sung was dismissed owing to lack
of evidence, and they were released on July 12. On the other
hand, we (the writer, Lieu You Ching and others) were charged
and committed for trial. On August 22 a verdict of "not
guilty" was handed down in my case, whilst Lieu You Ching
and four workers were sentenced each to 2 years and 7 months
imprisonment. I was discharged from jail on September 8
and returned to Shanghai the same evening.

My secret work after release

I was very careful after my release from jail. I
returned to Soochow for about a month, intending to stay
there and looked around for the purpose of carrying
off collections from my trunk. I took the 4 p.m. train and
alighted at Shangha Station. I took a ricksha to Hung Young
Road Bridge, Chapei, after which I reached my present address.
I can absolutely assure you that nobody could have followed
me. I am still very careful of my movements since my arrival
in Shanghai and I do not go out on the streets unless it is
necessary.

1934年3月2日于昌平路677号进行的突袭行动中查获之证物第108号译文

致“中央”及中央出版部，

我隶属中央出版部已久，我过去的工作和活动为本部同志们所熟知。兹就最近的“事件”以及我出狱后的行动提交简要报告如下：-

被捕原因

截至目前，我们仍不知晓被捕原因。根据某些工人和我个人的确信，这可能归因于以下原因：-
(1) 山西路泰安里18号的二房东提供的情报，因为此人与大龍发生过数次争吵，且他知道我们在做什么。他可能与公安局有某种联系。
(2) 老吴认识许多叛徒。他对自己的行踪不太谨慎，经常去他在大连路的家中。
(3) 周光言也认识印刷部的许多叛徒。工人们不知道秘密工作。例如，同时被捕的一名姓陈的人，是去18号找周光言讨还欠款的。没有工人说明陈是如何知道18号的。
(4) 云白和胡世清非常了解我们的出版部。由于他们已向国民党投降，情报可能是由他们提供的。

随后的逮捕

4月3日搜查了18号。随后搜查了101号，并将工人拘留。廣東佬于4月4日上午9时在18号被捕。刘友清和我于4月4日下午4时在57号被捕。我们在警察局遭受了严厉的审讯和酷刑。我们于4月12日被移交给公安局。5月28日，我们被移送至苏州高等法院进行预审。由于缺乏证据，针对廣東佬、周光言和宋的指控被撤销，他们于7月12日获释。另一方面，我们（作者、刘友清等人）被起诉并交付审判。8月22日，我的案件被判“无罪”，而刘友清和四名工人各被判处两年七个月监禁。我于9月8日出狱，并于当晚返回上海。

出狱后的秘密工作

出狱后我非常小心。我回到苏州约一个月，打算留在那里并寻找机会取出我箱子里的收藏品。我乘坐下午4点的火车，在上海站下车。我乘黄包车到闸北鸿兴路桥，随后到达我目前的地址。我可以绝对保证没有人跟踪我。自抵达上海以来，我对自己的行踪仍然非常谨慎，除非必要，否则不上街。

page_data.en:
( 2 )

Suggestions to the Party

The Party gained some experience from the split
which occurred this Spring. As a result, the Party has
improved its contact with its organizations and on this
account cases of obstruction to the Party have diminished.
However, the Party should reinstate those comrades who are
still firm in their political standing, after the Party
has made a thorough investigation about them. I request
the Party to consider my case.
The Party and the Mutual Aid Society is not doing
any work in the jail at Soochow and I request the Party
and the Society to consider this matter. A separate
letter on this subject has been forwarded to the Society.

Personal opinion about my work

Since my arrest I have naturally become known to
a number of detectives and renegades and on this account
I am not fit for secret work in Shanghai. I request the
Party to transfer me to Soviet Districts for publication
work.

Source of my financial support and expenses

My wife remitted me in all $240 from Szechuen. I
paid $140 for lawyer's fees. I spent $28 as travelling
and food expenses, etc. after leaving jail. I gave $15
to Kwang Tung Tuh and $17 to Lieu You Ching. I spent
$10 in jail. I had $30 upon my arrival in Shanghai.

With bolshevik greetings,
Tsen Chih Hoeng ( 左 觉 农 )
(alias Lieu Chi Wah 刘 祺 华 )
September 30, 1933.
page_data.zh:
( 2 )

给党的建议

党从今年春天发生的分裂中吸取了一些经验。因此，党改善了与其组织的联系，阻碍党的案件也因此减少。然而，党在对那些政治立场依然坚定的同志进行彻底调查后，应恢复他们的职务。我请求党考虑我的情况。
党和互济会在苏州监狱中没有开展任何工作，我请求党和互济会考虑此事。关于此事的另一封信已寄给互济会。

对我个人工作的意见

自从被捕以来，我自然被许多侦探和叛徒所知，因此我不适合在上海从事秘密工作。我请求党将我调往苏区从事出版工作。

我的经济支持和费用来源

我的妻子从四川总共汇给我240元。我支付了140元的律师费。出狱后，我花费28元作为旅费和伙食费等。我给了廣東佬15元，给了刘友清17元。我在狱中花费了10元。抵达上海时，我还有30元。

致以布尔什维克的问候，
左觉农 ( Tsen Chih Hoeng )
(化名 刘祺华 Lieu Chi Wah )
1933年9月30日。

A RAID CONDUCTED AT 80, 577 CHANGPING ROAD ON MARCH 2, 1934.

"Central" of the Chinese Communist Party,

(1) For the past six months no letters, publications
and labour-peasant correspondence have been received. Why?

(2) The address to which publications should be sent
is :

(3) To what address shall we send you local
publications and grey-coloured mosquito papers?

(4) Hsu Sz Tsong(许安忠), son of Hsu Tso Shuan
(许卓然), a politician in Fukien, who went to the
Philippines from Fukien during the Party purification
movement and who later proceeded to Moscow to continue
his studies, is now back in the Islands. According to
Zung Lih(永烈), he is a suspicious person. We hope
"Central" will find out for us and let us know by writing.

(5) We ask you to send us regularly the "Red Flag",
the "Bolshevik Paper" and other publications of the Party.
We are urgently in need of assistance from China. The
Chinese Section of the American Communist Party has also
sent a letter with the hope that you will supply them
with as many publications as possible.

(6) Comrade Kau Zung Lih(高永烈) - Lee Vung(黎文) -
has left for Shanghai. He has the address of the
"Central". It is said that he has been called back
to China owing to the danger of his arrest.

(7) Formerly we decided to send Comrade Kau to
Java to be a Dean of a school for the purpose of
maintaining Party work there, because once the position
of Dean was lost, the rest of the comrades (teachers)
would be dismissed. The conditions are that the Dean
must be a Fokienese and a university graduate. If
"Central" can now find a Fokienese comrade to take the
position of Dean, you may retain him (Kau ?) in Shanghai
to give him some training.

(8) You can send us letters by the new method;
in future we shall employ same.

(9) Please use new address after sending letter.

Chinese Overseas Bureau
of the
Central
of the
Philippine Communist Party.

Received 5/4.

1934年3月2日于昌平路577号80室进行的突袭行动中查获之证物第110号译文。

中国共产党“中央”，

(1) 过去六个月未收到信件、出版物和工农通讯。为什么？

(2) 出版物应寄送的地址是：

(3) 我们应该将地方出版物和灰色蚊子纸寄到什么地址给你们？

(4) 许安忠，福建政客许卓然之子，在党内肃反运动期间从福建前往菲律宾，随后前往莫斯科继续学业，现已回到群岛。据高永烈称，他是一个可疑人物。我们希望“中央”为我们查明并通过写信告知我们。

(5) 我们要求你们定期寄送《红旗》、《布尔什维克报》和其他党的出版物。我们急需来自中国的援助。美国共产党中国分部也寄来一封信，希望你们能尽可能多地向他们提供出版物。

(6) 高永烈同志 - 黎文 - 已前往上海。他有“中央”的地址。据说他因面临被捕危险而被召回中国。

(7) 以前我们决定派遣高同志去爪哇担任一所学校的校长，以维持那里的党务工作，因为一旦校长职位丢失，其余同志（教师）将被解雇。条件是校长必须是福建人且拥有大学学历。如果“中央”现在能找到一位福建同志担任校长职位，你们可以将他（高？）留在上海给他一些培训。

(8) 你们可以通过新方法给我们寄信；今后我们将采用相同的方法。

(9) 寄信后请使用新地址。

菲律宾共产党
中央
海外局

4月5日收悉。

TRANSLATION OF EXHIBIT NO. 115 SEIZED AT NO.677 CHANGPING
ROAD ON MARCH 2, 1934.

Central :-

I submit hereunder, as instructed, a report on
my activities.

Subsequent to my return from Moscow, most of my
time was spent either abroad or in prison. The time I
actually spent working in China was about 4 or 5 months
in Shanghai Western District and about 2 or 3 months in
Amoy. In view of the fact that my actual working period
was very short, my report is of little worth.

When I was transferred from the Shanghai Western
District by Central, I was requested to make a report on
my work. I complied with the order but I have not received
a reply so far.

On my arrival in Shanghai from Fokien, I again
submitted a report on my activities in that province, but
again I have received no reply from Central.

I feel that I have the right to express my
personal thoughts as to my period in the Party. Whilst
attached to the Shanghai Western District, I detected, by
my vigilance, that the route taken by the Party was not
correct, but I could not continue to struggle with the
bad leadership of the Party. I did not disagree with
the Party policy face to face with the "Lih San Route".
This point I frankly admit is my mistake. I believe
that mistakes cannot be avoided, but I hope that under
the assistance and correction of the Party I shall be
able to refrain from making further mistakes.

Doo Tsiang Ling(杜樟林) - 31st day.

(My old name is known to many renegades
and persons outside the Party, there-
fore, I have discontinued using it.
I am now using the above name and hope
the Party will take note of it and put
it on record.)
page_data.zh:
1934年3月2日在昌平路677号查获的第115号证物译文。

中央：

兹遵照指示，呈报本人活动情况。

自莫斯科返回后，我大部分时间要么在国外，要么在狱中。我在中国实际工作的时间，在上海西区约为四至五个月，在厦门约为两至三个月。鉴于实际工作时间甚短，本报告价值不大。

当我被中央从上海西区调离时，曾要求我提交工作报告。我遵令提交，但至今未获回复。

我从福建抵达上海后，再次提交了在该省活动的报告，但同样未收到中央的回复。

我觉得我有权利就我在党内的时期表达个人想法。在上海西区工作期间，我通过警惕观察，发现党的路线不正确，但我无法继续与党的不良领导进行斗争。面对“立三路线”，我并未当面反对党的政策。这一点我坦承是我的错误。我相信错误不可避免，但我希望在党的帮助和纠正下，能够避免再犯错误。

杜樟林 - 31日。

（我的旧名为许多叛徒及党外人士所知，因此我已停止使用。现改用上述名字，希望党予以注意并记录在案。）

Plan of activities to be carried out during the month of
August by the Tse Toong District Committee.

1. The District Committees
a) The District Secretary will supervise the Women's Section
inner communication section, joint meetings to be convened
by members of the C.Y. League, Labour Unions and the Party,
and undertake the Hung Foong, the Sung Sing No 7, the San
Sing and the Shanghai No 5 Cotton Mills,
b) The Chief of the Organisation Department will supervise the
unemployed, the Mutual Aid Society and the Executive Offices
of the Organisation Department. He will undertake the
Sung Sing ? ( No 7 ), the Sung Sing No 9 , the Wing On ,
the Middle Steel and the Wei Tung Mills and Factories. The
executive offices of the Organisation Department will
undertake the 'Egg Factory', The Shanghai No 2 and 3 Cotton
Mills, wheelbarrow coolies and soap factories.
c) The chief of the Propaganda Department will supervise
mimeograph printings as well as training and reading classes.
he will undertake the Shanghai No 1 Mill, the New Ewo, the
Old Ewo and the Sung Sing No 5 Mill.
d) The Chief of the Unemployment Department XXXXXXXXXXXX
will supervise the Unemployment Committee and its executive
officers, and undertakes the San Yeu, the Hung Kyieh, the
Tsiang (? Soy shops), the Whangs, the Sien and the Shanghai
No. 4 industrial workers.
The Unemployment Executive Officers look after the Fah
Doh Yuen, Sung Tung Li, Sung Zung and San Dah Dou localities.
e) The Chief of the Women's Department will supervise the
female workers of the Dah Kung, Kung Dah, Wei Tung, Sung Sing
No. 7 and the Hung Foong industrial concerns as well as the
women's departments of various public bodies, the Shanghai Hoi
and No. 1 Cotton Mills.
f) Mimeograph printing section.
g) Publication Department.
h) Inner communication.

2. STRIKES
1. The struggles in the Electric Factory (? Shanghai Power Co.)
(a) The old members of the Party should convene from time to
to time section meetings during which every comrade should be
urged to give his own opinion regarding the activities performed
(b) To intensify the anti-Yellow Labour Union movement.
(c) To absorb 6 new men into the Party during this month.
(d) Extend the organisation of various labour bodies or
associations.
2. The struggles in the Sun Fua Towel Factory.
(a) Extend the organisation of the workers.
(b) Intensify the anti-Yellow Labour Union activities.
(c) The District Committee should energetically carry out
decided measures in connection with the struggle (to
occupy the godown, confiscate and auction the goods
stored there.)
3. The struggles in the Sung Sing No. 9 Cotton Mill:-
(a) To demand removal allowances from the management. A portion
of the machinery of this mill has been removed.
4. The struggles in the Sung Sing No. 7 Mill:-
Send party organisers and others who are not into the party
among the masses of the strikers.
Other activities
Extend and strengthen mass organizations.
Lead the daily struggles of workers.
Recruit new comrades.
Continue the struggle against the reduction of work.
